Full disclosure; I am a full time electrician, installing smart meters 5-6 days a week, but I am not qualified to install solar myself. review_description: Contacted Amazon Energy to install a battery (30kWh Midea Hiconics) and 6.6kW solar panel system. An interesting and ultimately good experience with Amazon Energy.They responded very quickly with a couple of similar options and I decided to go with the FoxEss system they offered - 6.6kW of Solar Panels, 5.5kW inverter and ~14kWh of battery - as this seemed the most appropriate.Also useful to know that it was the cheapest quote I got in terms of cost per kWh of batteries - this system was basically the same price as an alternative with a 10kWh battery.Since we use most of our power in the morning and then again in the evening I was keen to ensure we had enough storage to best use the power generated.I have previously installed 2 solar systems (without batteries) in 2011 and 2015 so have a good understanding of the generation vs use time patterns.Amazon were also quick to lock in an installation day - Monday 27 October 8am.On the day I got a message at 8.15am saying that the sales person's car had broken down but "the installers should be there" - they weren't. After replying that no one had arrived we heard they were stuck in traffic. I then found out there had been a bad accident at the Freeway exit and so understood why they were late. Unfortunately, as they didn't arrive until around 10.00am they were unable to finish on the day and said they would return on the next day.That afternoon I got an email requesting a review and payment, I answered that it was a bit premature for either.I again expected them at 8am, and arranged to work from home. They arrived at 9am and started work.At around 1pm they said they were nearly finished and started turning the system on. They got me on the app and linked to the inverter and I immediately saw that there was something wrong. Apparently the house was using 10kW, with only a fridge turned on I knew that was impossible. The team were obviously keen to get away and tried to tell me it was nothing to do with them as all they had done was remove the old solar and installed the new system and had not touched anything in the house. With the old 3kW system I knew that generally between 10am and 2pm we were exporting excess energy, so I explained that I didn't agree with them and that they needed to stay and sort the problem out. We then isolated several circuits and at one point discovered that the house was apparently exporting 10kW of power in addition to the 5kW being produced by the panels at the time. It was at this point that the electrician agreed something was wrong. They then called the Fox back up team and quickly found out that they had mis-wired the smart meter. This was quickly corrected (although the mistake was not explained to me initially) and the system was finally commissioned at around 3.30pm.On Tuesday I received another request for payment, to which I replied that I would like to understand the problem, and fix, and to make sure that the system was indeed safe and working properly before making payment.Amazon followed up with a call on Friday where we discussed the issues in more detail, for which I am grateful.They also sent through the Electrical Safety Certificate confirming that everything had been checked and installed correctly.Since Tuesday afternoon we have been 100% self-sufficient in our electrical use. The battery is generally fully charged by around 1.30pm and we then export to the grid. Overnight the battery is discharging to somewhere between 30-50% at the moment although I expect that to increase once we start using the aircon.I am very happy with the system, and although we had a couple of issues wiht the installation, it did get resolved appropriately.Thanks Amazon Team. I am happy to recommend you to others.

Mondiaux were a great company to deal with from the get go. They provided us with a variety of options for our house and explained everything clearly. Customer service was helpful and informative throughout the process. The installers were prompt, polite and professional. Would highly recommend.

I just thought it important to share that Mondiaux after installation service was excellent - they are prompt, professional and spend time in providing details on what was causing the problem.I was very happy with the installation and the service levels have continued even after the sale.Great work Mondiaux!

I am very happy with my Mondiaux sales and installation, and with the Alpha Ess inverter and batter so far.I found the process of understanding all the options and possibilities and choosing a system quite a big job. Having backup power was important to me, so I wanted a system with a battery. The Mondiaux salesperson spent time answering all of my questions and put together a quote and package that contained everything I wanted at a reasonable price.The process was held up by covid shutdowns and the impact on workforce, unsurprisingly, but once it was booked in, the installation team worked very hard to put the system in and did a good job. The follow-up service to commission the system and make sure everything was right was very good.The main problems I had were that the backup circuit was not completed at the time of the installation. I followed up with the sales person and the staff member who came to commission the system, and the backup circuit was installed about a fortnight later. It would have been good to have some clearer advice about the load the backup circuits could take, and what that would mean for my decision about where I wanted the backup. While I knew what my priorities were (fridge and internet), I hadn't known all of the factors involved, and would have made a different choice with better information.There was a faulty LED on the battery display, which the staff member identified and arranged to have replaced. So while the process took a bit longer and wasn't as smooth as it could have been, the company did respond to my follow-up queries and now everything is complete and working well. Very satsifying.
Every thing was excellent Mondiaux Pty Ltd  are a high quality provider

The initial design and quoting process was really well managed and questions were very quickly and comprehensively addressed. Also fine tuning of the proposal was quickly incorporated ready for the next phase of our process. Especially given the flash lockdown due COVID outbreak right in the middle!We wanted to take advantage of the ACT Governments new interest free Green Load opportunity, which Mondiaux helped as much as they could, unfortunately the application and approval really slow progress due to external factors (Christmas break, COVID lock-downs and the high number of applications) and the program has only just opened so was a rough and ready to start with... Not in any way a Mondiaux issue and they tried really hard to help, where they could.Once approved, Mondiaux locked in the installation within days and were happy to change dates due to our scheduling conflict.Installation was done really quickly and professionally, the team was really friendly and careful. Our roof is 50 years old and they only had 3 tile breakages and nothing else was scratched, broken or messed with! Really pleased.All the STS and Doco was done quickly and accurately and the the grid connection/meter change was very quickly organised. The set up of the monitoring/management software was done a week after the installation.We are exceptionally pleased with how everything has worked out except one point:As we had been in lockdown, none-one had actually been onsite to make sure battery location, panel location and roof condition and trees etc were all OK before we starting installing. Once lockdown was lifted, I requested Mondiaux do a site check before installation.Unfortunately the site check was promised multiple times but never happened. The installation team and I then had to sort out a few things that could easily have been avoided or done differently. They were very supportive and prepared to make adjustments "on the go'' but it could have easily gone very badly!

Reaching an agreed qoute took a bit of time due to modification upgrades I wanted. Solar panel installation went well and is working I guess the best it can due to the inclement weather. The company arranged grid connection.
Every step of the way was professional and punctual. They did help with the grid connection
Overall the service was OK.  The installation was much slower and delayed tan I thought but that is mainly due to the min-bending government paperwork

I have read many reviews that immediately after installation where users write about how good their system is, a euphoric reaction written before the system has barely bedded itself in. When maybe the true gauge of a company's rating is the ease in which problems are acknowledged and acted upon. Solar systems like any other complicated electrical system are going to have issues over their lifecycle.Engaging ShineHub after much praise from my local council and a slick product presentation appeared to be a sure thing. The mayor was even there spruiking the wares of ShineHub on the info night.The sales and installation process is very professional. That occurred 3 months ago and soon after commissioning the system has had issues with the power meter.Phone calls to their call centre rarely get through, messages left for callback are not returned. you soon realise that it is a automated system with little monitoring by the actual company. When I finally get through, I was told I'd have to wait at least 2 to 3 weeks before anyone was available. Finally 3 weeks later I received a text with a date for repair that I was unable to be available for as I was interstate. I suggested a time only 2 days later than the date they proposed but I never heard back from them.They then closed the ticket and I once again went through the lotto of trying to get them to answer my calls to reopen the ticket, which eventually they did.I now request callbacks for up dates on progress for resolution - they tell me they are working on it, I ask to speak to a supervisor, they tell me that one isn't available but they are actively trying to solve my problem, which ironically needs someone on site.The problem with some companies is they have no real interest in the quality operation of your system. They are not solar system companies. They are more interested in the finance and sales. And a fast buck creating quasi VPP companiesSystem reliability is is an irritating part of them doing business.In short I paid ShineHub around $15 000 for a 6.6 kW solar and 10 kW battery system that has not worked to spec since installation and they do not care.Buyer beware.

Our experience with Shinehub from the original contact person (Ethan) to the installation team and general customer service staff have been faultless, our solar panels and battery were installed 3 weeks ago without a hitch. They tidied up following their work each day and were a pleasure to deal with. The three quotes we got, one was the best for price and service, although we went with Shinehub.

Attended a VPP presentation on the benefits of Solar panels and batteries presented by the local council / Shine.The lack of clarity on T&C’s caused me concern, but it was explained that these conditions would be opened once l started the process of signing up!When l started the signing up process, l found one clause regarding the VPP subsidy from Shine to be a little disconcerting, but managed to get a dispensation on that one and signed up.The process after this little hiccup was very fast and smooth - only a battery/ inverter purchasedOne little issue on installation was corrected very quickly, once Shine acknowledged they were  at fault.Once system was operating, the BIG SURPRISE  to me was the extent that l could control the charging /discharge.  My energy retailer has off peak rates so l can fully charge battery on cheap rates (when daily PV input is low) - it’s a very small version of the proposed snowy scheme. well done Shine

Grant Ferry made it so easy for us to get batteries for our solar panels.  Effortless, seamless and so easy to deal with with.  He has a friendly and professional manner and everything was sorted out for us very efficiently.  We will be saving so much money thanks to Grant and Shinehub.  The backup and support is second to none. Thank you so much Grant.

How was the sales/quoting process? Easy, no hassle. Lots of information given and plenty of opportunity to ask questions.How did the installation go? Installation was easy. I heard of shinehub from a friend's friend, when I called I spoke with Tom he talked me all the way through it, and was a no pressure salesmen, I came to the decision very quickly and decided on the interest free payments for 130 fortnight's.A site inspection was ordered and from there it was all organised and everything booked in..the electricians were easy to speak to and arrived on time and called to ask if they could attend early and were finished with in 5 hours from start to finish and cleaned up as they went, I would recommend these guys to anyone and looking forward to big savings on my bills and I'll put the extra into paying it off faster..

Ben from Shinehub was extremely polite and affirming from the sales perspective and everything is extremely easy from start to finish, but as others have mentioned, there is a lack of continuity from one service desk staff member to another, and this could be disjointing if you have complex needs. From what I can gather, the systems represent great value and the payment options are good, but there are definitely a few things that you forgo for the good price - and that's just a reality of getting what you pay for. On the other hand, if you want something basic and good to go, at a good price, then ShineHub is a great option. The less fuss you make, the less fuss you'll have and that might not be great service from one perspective, but it's good enough for those who are teetering on the edge of getting solar or not, and who just want a basic battery and panel system. My advice is if you care about smart home features, or data security, or have complex needs, find somewhere else and pay for it. But if you don't know much about solar, or care much about features you wouldn't know you're missing (unless you're doing a lot of research, and then continue to care about when the system is in), then Shinehub is for you.

ShineHub solar system is best in all other solar systems, ShineHub installs battery for at  night use and battery solar package is best for to save money, when Sun is not shining,Their system is fantastic, technicians are expert and helpful and SHINEHUB company is well known and their TECHNICAL TEAM is friendly and helpful.Said.

This was such a smooth process. From the initial phone consultation with Jack to the installation with Russell to the day the solar was switched on.I really can’t fault the customer service as they were just a telephone call or email away. Sales was a smooth process, my consultant Jonathan methodically went through my usage and what system would be the best fit for my home and the company delivered with friendly and punctual installers who didn't waste time.

Thanks to Thomas & team to introduce, consult &install outstanding, beneficial & value for money 13.3Kw system, free electricity day& night plus credit every day. Don't missed out this life changing opportunity to have this valuable investment, will achieve money back in no time. Currently got some friends onboard, cheers Long (SA)

I had an existing solar system which was 8 years old and with the purchase of a new Tesla Model 3, I thought it was time to upgrade my roof top solar and add a battery.I engaged Shine Hub for 3 projects:-* Add a new Alpha ESS battery with 10KwH* Installation of a new 5KW solar to expand my existing 5KW and Solar Analytics solution* Add a 2nd Alpha ESS battery with an additional 10KwHFrom the outset I explained to Shine Hub, that I have 3 properties with solar and batteries and that it was important for me to collect all the information in a single application (Solar Analytics), not spread across multiple vendors and apps.This was all verbally agreed in the first call and I paid for the first two projects to proceed.Wow, I wish I hadn't agreed. Their customer service is appalling and their project management skills terrible.Basic project management skills 101, like checking the customer is available on the days the installers are onsite are overlooked.Your assigned "Project Manager" is different every time you speak to them. Hand over between sales and engineering is almost non-existent, and I couldn't even pay the for their time to speak to Solar Analytics. As my "trusted" solar and battery installer, they repeatedly refused to speak to my trust solar analytics company.Massively frustrating to deal with and being on hold for over a hour to call them is terrible. Their project managers seem incapable of resolving issues or even being helpful. They must be absolute juniors or I just got unlucky 3 times in a row?They provide a website interface to log and schedule work, however, they won't write any responses to issues you raise, because they don't want it recorded that they've made a mistake. The "Report fault" button doesn't even work.So first battery installation project was disappointing... Second project, upgrade solar panels was a complete disaster. They delivered faulty equipment and left the job incomplete. It's taken 16 days to get "working" equipment brought to site. After 2 weeks of pressing them for updates, they finally schedule a date I wasn't supposed to be home and notified me of this, the day before the installers arrived. I had to reschedule my entire day.I put a complaint in to their management and I got a much less than sympathetic response, informing me of their staffing and supply issues in March 2021. "Not my problem", I thought! So day 16 and 2 installers later, and I'm still left with a non-function system and no offer of compensation or priority in resolving the issue.I've now cancelled the 3rd project to expand my battery system with them. They've eroded all my faith in them.

So, Shinehub is an interesting one. They have decent sales, but once you've committed, their whole stance changes - they know they've got you in, and they don't care about their service anywhere near as much after that point.They don't seem to know much about the technical details. I wish I had just decided to pull out when they couldn't answer some questions (simply about 'does the inverter have local API access?').They did, however, organise /everything/. I just had to let them in to install the solar panels, the inverters and the battery. The physical installation was pretty good, even though the installers were short handed.Now the problems start. The Kehua inverter sends data to China. So I've switched off that network access. The Alpha ESS battery sends data to a system hosted in Singapore, in clear text (no encryption), or useful authentication. Apparently according to Shinehub/Powow, they see no issues with this. This data includes my home address, along with control of the battery.The Solus inverter is not (obviously) connected to my own wireless network, so I can't rate that.I highly recommened NOT getting the Kehua inverter or the Alpha ESS battery system, as the latter is completely insecure. Oh, and it has no API access, so good luck trying to hook it in with any home automation systems.I knew I should've not assumed there would be API access. I guess I learned the hard way, and should've gone with the companies that Solarquotes sent my way instead - I wouldn't have had a battery, but then, I probably also wouldn't have an awfully insecure system either.

I would like to warn other of my bad experience

Solar panels and battery backup.Over $4000. Cheaper than nearest quote.Installer's were excellent. Company contact not so good, but follow up has been mutch better. System is working perfectly as it should for a new system.

The initial quote process etc with them was solid. Kept in touch etc. Then they "went overseas, travelling" and I was assigned another contact, who I did not hear from at any point, I had to liaise with them to get some information. I'm disappointed......At my previous property, I had a Tesla Powerwall 2 - it provided automatic backup on mains/grid failure, and the solar panels kept working.The Shinehub system, with 2 x 10.1KwH batteries, requires manual switching on mains powerful, and solar panels cease working......To be fair, the later issue (existing solar panels ceasing) is because i have two submarines- solar panels on one (on the shed), and the Shinehub battery on the other (house).Shinehub did a pre-instal inspection and noted my expectations.....but the installation did not deliver.....Shinehub did a pre-instal inspection and noted my expectations.....but the installation did not deliver.....The Tesla Powerwall offered fuil backup....Shinehub (so I've now discovered) only provided for lights, the fridge circuit and the modem circuit...Very disappointed.

But Cameron at Evo Solar had the time and professionalism to explain each part of the system and why he designed the system around getting the most out of the battery. I have seen a lot of crap that has been installed on some people's houses that do not work properly and did not want that on my house. From start to finish I felt comfortable dealing with Evo Solar, Ros in the office was awesome answering any queries andcompleting all paperwork. And Travers and the guys were awesome with the installation everyone there at Evo were incredible at the end l got a email from Toni and Ivy with a custom manual designed for my system telling you the components of my installation how it's wired, how to maintain it and at what intervals, who worked on it. I have had the system for a month now and had no issues, very clean installation and everyone was great to deal with. I have recommended them to my family and friends.I am very happy with the whole process in dealing with Cameron and everyone at Evo Solar.Definitely worth getting a Evo Solar system.

Great process from start to finish. Quotes obtained within a week and decision made, a couple of months waiting for the batteries to arrive and then all installed with minimal disruption in a day and a half. In addition to very good service and price Darren also removed and took away previous solar system at no cost.

The whole process was very easy and simple.I would definitely recommend Positive Energy Solutions to anyone considering purchasing a new system or upgrading their older system.

Sadly I find myself here writing a review after being sold a rather premium priced 3kw system in late 2016 and 6 years later when the panels started shattering  finding the warranty worthless as the panel manufacturer had gone broke. After the 3rd of 12 original panels failed,  a long list of empty promises by Perth Solar Warehouse and even the inability to return calls when I suggested I was considering replacing the system with one including a battery I gave up on attempting to deal with them and started the adventure to install a new and improved system.Sadly when you have a 2 story townhouse with a smaller more complicated roof plan many installers seem happy to write down a very generic set of specs with a big price tag they know won’t fit and hope you go away. So after a few false starts I had the pleasure of meeting Louis from Positive Energy.Having not long added an EV to the garage and wanting to add a battery made for rather a challenge to design a system that would produce enough power but also fit and make use of the roof space that faces SE/SW that would usually be ignored by most installers. At our first meeting Louis had 3 different system designs with alternative batteries for each design and a few panel options at a significant discount. It was refreshing to see someone that knew all the products he was offering inside out and wanted to sell the right option for me rather than what was most profitable like many others would.At the time Tesla Powerwall 3 was just going through the approvals process and we decided to go that way as the combined inverter battery makes for a neat install and I was very much sold on the LFP chemistry for any battery that was going to live in my garage over NMC.Cut to a few weeks later and Hiroshi the electrician/installer came round with his tape measure and had to break the news that 5 of the panels were just not going to fit which would result in a drop in output of nearly 20% from the original design. Thankfully Louis had the patience of a saint and continued to come up with alternatives including some larger commercial panels but nothing was quite right. We were now well inside a month from install date and still struggling to find a panel with a high enough output, small enough dimensions to work and available before the install date. Our saviour came in the form of Aiko 475w panels available with a whole week to spare. Cutting it fine to say the least.Our final system Tesla Powerwall 3, 23 Aiko panels for 10.9kw ( 7 of which face SE/SW ) a heap of optimisers and a system that is exceeding expectations by huge margins. Synergy in their wisdom hobble ALL inverters on single phase to 5kw but as long as the battery is not full it will charge above this limit. To keep it simple I can draw the full 5kw for the house and the battery will pull up to 5kw above this. Creating this situation has seen stable solar production peaks of 9.7kw for nearly an hour on the days I actually managed to not fill the battery before 11am. Once the battery is full the system winds down to about 5.2kw for the rest of the day. Biggest days total production 60kw and consistently over 50kw even when the battery is full  well before midday.As for those panels pointing the “wrong way” they are helping me to see 1kw less than 40min after sunrise and not dropping below 1kw until just over an hour before sunset which really helps the battery through the night when I leave both aircon’s going all night.Can’t thank Louis and Hiroshi enough. System is brilliant, the install is incredibly neat and tidy, and their customer service and professionalism fantastic. review_description: From the moment I was contacted by the representative from Jim's Energy, I felt reassured that I could obtain both the government rebate and the energy system I was looking for. They took care of everything, from the application process with Energex to the commissioning of the batteries. I highly recommend reaching out to them.

No extra cost was added, but it was sprung on me last minute and not explained at all to me how this would function.As part of this new inverter being added, the position and layout of the solar panels were also changed, moving 5 of the 21 solar panels from the main group of north facing panels to somewhere else tied into that second inverter instead.Once the install had been done, I was only then told that the second inverter with a quarter of the solar panels in the system on it, would not charge the battery and only be used for exporting and powering the house. At no point during the entire process of quoting, changing specs, agreeing and then scheduling the install was this explained to me. If it had been, I would've stopped the process there and not continued, because that's not at all how it was explained to me to work during the process. I bought a battery to be charged by all the solar panels, not only by some of them.The installer also left all their rubbish on my property which took me months to get rid of and a paid trip to the dump. Not happy with that at all.At this point I feel like I've only received a system 75% of what I want and agreed to, yet paying full price for it.At this point, I figured that's where the issues would stop, but they did not. The process to get the solar export approval has been, and still is ongoing, 3 months after the system was inspected and turned on.The installer seems to be constantly lying to me, blaming Powercor for having the wrong electricity provider in their systems, but when I called Powercor, they confirmed it has the right provider in their systems for a long time now, and that they have never received any applications for export approval.This is entirely on Jims Energy to resolve, and I constantly am reminding them to follow it up for months now, and nothing ever comes back. It's been, and still is extremely frustrating to get things sorted with them.Then to top it all off, the solar installer that was contracted out by Jims Energy to do the install called me at 10pm one night trying to get money out of me, saying Jims had not paid them, so I had the contractor coming to me trying to get money out of me or get me to sort out why he wasn't paid, which is completely unacceptable and something that should never be coming back to me.To be fair, the solar installation has been working great and exceeding promised production, but for the hassles and lies I was sold on and system not delivered as promised, I wouldn't recommend to anyone.

review_description: I received 3 quotations in response to my solicitations, 2 of which were competitive in terms of price, product quality etc. I then followed up with an site meeting, a discussion regarding the timing of the work, specifications, rooftop layout, positioning of inverter & so forthTo be honest we could have proceeded with either firms. The decision to run with Apex was down to the 60/40 split of the 22 panels to maximise the solar harvesting Sun up/down, the relocation of the new smart inverter from a gyprock wall in the garage to a brick wall (for added safety) and the polite/courteous manner of the sales person initially and, subsequently, the Apex team who were on site for 2 days. Day 1 was primarily spent removing the then existing system and preparing the additional cabling due to the resiting of the inverter. Unlike the other businesses the Apex electrician insisted on the new cabling being hidden within the ceiling voids rather than being visible. A nice gesture!Initially I reacted adversely to the battery sited on the garage floor rather than the more common siting hung on the wall near the inverter (visions of the Tesla power wall). Once the electrician pointed out the benefits of being able to add more storage on the stacked module I realised the obvious benefit. As an aside it is silent and operates without emitting heat. Neighbours' power walls emit a hum or buzz  & are fitted to external masonry walls. With houses now being erected almost gutter to gutter this is an important consideration for some folk.In summary, the answer to all of your questions is YES, noting that this system has been operational for just 14 days. Allow for around 42 days from the time you pay the 10% deposit to installation. Our battery was activated at 4:10 PM on the Monday and at 8:30 AM the next day the battery was fully charged. We were impressed by Apex.

review_description: I spent a bit of time researching the ideal system for my needs and Tim from Apex was happy to accomodate. He's very knowledgable and experienced and provided me some great recommendations. I selected them under the assumption Tim would be there on the day of install. The day arrived and he was unable to attend. The roofers and electricians were apparently unaware of everything Tim an I had discussed. I was questioned why I'd want a network cable ran from the inverter and told they only had a bulky meter box to install. I briefly ran the roofers through the panel placement and selected a great spot for the inverter and battery install with the help of the electricians.The panel install by the roofers was completed in half a day, the roofers left without saying goodbye or offering an inspection of the work. I was disappointed to see the panel placement wasn't optimised for for the path of the sun. Some sort of sealant was also spilled on the roof without my knowledge. Zip ties were still being found in my yard months after the install.The electricians spent the entire day doing the inverter, battery and wiring installation. It was getting close to 5pm and the electricians informed me that there was a black out (what are the odds) and would be unable to finish commissioning the inverter. They told me that someone else, maybe not them, would be back sometime to finish it off. I asked if power would be restored to the house when the black out ends, I was assured yes it would. Hours went by and I noticed neighbours lights turning on as it got dark. I checked the meter box at the front of the property and grid power was restored, but not to the house Turns out they forgot to switch the main meter back on after leaving...The next day was spent on the phone to Tim as he apologised and walked me through the commissioning which, thankfully, I was able to do myself. The system was up and running... sort of. I soon discovered the inverter throwing "over voltage" errors which would cause the system to shut down for up to an hour at a time. Turns out the voltage coming back from the grid was over the "safe" limits and would have to be fixed by the wholesaler. Tim's team lodged a fault and it was fixed up a couple of months later. I believe this should have been checked before the install.The next issue came upon inspecting the wiring that was done under the house. Bare wires were bundled together that drooped and cut corners. Insulation was ripped out and left on the ground. It looked very unprofessional. Tim did return with the electrician who did it initially and instructed him to fix it up while he tested the previously mentioned over voltage issue. Unfortunately it still wasn't good enough. I contacted Apex again and requested it be done with conduit. I paid extra for the required materials.Months went by, the grid voltage issue now fixed I continued to experience more voltage issues, where the system would shut down for up to an hour at a time. I did a lot of back and forth with Apex and then directly with Fronius. In the end I was able to determine the voltage was too high on one of the strings and Fronius informed me that the 12x REC 440W panels had been configured incorrectly, voiding the warranty of the inverter. I let Apex know and they promptly came out and fixed it. Since then the system has been solid. Unfortunately this took 1 year to fully resolve.As it stands, I have a solid system I am happy with. The panel placement on the West-facing roof is still not ideal, however. The meter box is installed in a room and makes a constant HUMMMM which is apparently normal (??).I'd recommend Apex but only if you get everything in writing beforehand: Panel placement, meter box type and size, double check the configuration, agree on wiring and inverter placement. Check grid voltage well before the install date. Insist Tim is there on the install date. Avoid a year of headaches like me.

review_description: We are located on NSW mid-north coast - there are installers around, but very few are registered with Solar Quotes. The whole process of design through to installation has been a breeze:  Tim and Gemma and their team have been so easy to deal with, so helpful, and the performance of their solution for our south-facing hill which is shaded by trees has exceeded expectations.  From the start, Tim was able to design a system which met our requirements - we are grid-connected but subject to intermittent black-outs, and wanted to avoid products that have been flagged as manufactured with slave labour (sadly, products from some countries are affected).  Tim rose to the challenges and six weeks after midwinter, we have a system which is meeting household requirements with minimal purchase from the grid.  Eight weeks after midwinter, we are re-charging batteries fully and exporting to the grid - not that export makes any money, but there are feel-good benefits!  Overall, we experienced none of the pitfalls of shoddy manufacture, design or installation which were raised recently by ABC news coverage.  So the message is, don't hesitate to install panels and batteries if you can rely upon a quality installer like Apex.  Hope that the underlying enthusiasm doesn't make me sound like I've been taken hostage by a cult!

I had a 32.2kWh SiG battery system installed to my 14.8 kwh existing solar panels in mid-April 2025 this year. While the battery itself has performed reliably, the sales experience has been deeply disappointing and dishonest.During the consultation, the salesperson, sold me a 10kWh 3-phase inverter without conducting any proper assessment of my household’s energy usage or load profile.At no stage did they ask about my major appliances, including the single-phase reverse-cycle air conditioner, or explain the limitations of a 3-phase inverter when it comes to powering single-phase loads.After complete installation, I noticed that despite having ample of stored battery power, my AC would continue drawing 1.32kWh from the grid when in use. Through several escalations, a senior manager eventually visited and confirmed the issue: the 3-phase 10 Kwh inverter could not supply enough current amps on a single phase to run the AC, forcing the system to draw from the grid—even though the battery was full.Despite admitting this issue, the company offered no concessions or try to sell this and offer the upgrade. I was told they are not responsible for checking customers’ load configurations. While I understand that customers bear some responsibility to understand their systems, a basic discussion about appliance compatibility and system suitability should be standard in the sales process, especially when selling to customers without any electrical background.Sales seemed more focused on closing the sale for commission than offering a tailored solution.Now, four months after installation, I’m facing the cost of upgrading to a 15kWh 3-phase inverter, which multiple independent solar companies have confirmed should have at least been recommended in the first place.To the SolarQuotes team. I respectfully ask that this review remain published in full. This is an honest account of my experience and I believe it’s important for other homeowners to be aware of potential pitfalls when dealing with sales people from this installer. While the SiG battery itself is a great product, the lack of due diligence during the sales process was extremely poor.

Such a huge variance, and yet i couldn't find any justification for why they were worth more except "you get what you pay for" o.OOnce i whittled it down to about 5, it was time to start making some calls, and getting inspections. After some inspections, and some more follow up calls, it was clear Jet Solar was the installer to with. I called the other companies on the short list to thank them for their interest, and efforts, but that i was going with another installer. A few of the companies appreciated this courtesy, which in turn pleased me.Jet Solar in fact was the only installer who UNDER-sold me, as i originally thought of going for Sunpower's Maxeon panels, but it became apparent they simply were not worth the extra $10k compared to something like Jinko's Tiger Neo panels, or equivalent like Sunpower's own cheaper "Performance" panels.I could justify the extra outlay for micro-inverters over string inverters, but paying $10k on top of the $35k for just a "slightly better panel" that would barely show up in error margins for solar generation simply didn't make sense in the end.Adam at Jet Solar practically refused to let me buy the Maxeon's telling me "it's not worth it", because that for the extra 1% of efficiency they offer it's simply not worth paying an extra $10k when i have enough roof space to simply put a few more cheaper panels to make the difference in generation, then pocket the difference. Well, that sold me, i've never had a company undersell me before, so that told me Jet Solar were serious about prioritising customer satisfaction instead of "profits above all else".Jet Solar designed a beautiful panel layout, with tilted sections of the array on my roof spreading the generation throughout the day, instead of putting them all flat and simply concentrating the generation for a few peak hours around noon.  Titled panels mean they will "self drain" rainwater (and the dirt it carries, or "soiling") keeping them cleaner for longer, which in turn means i have to monkey my butt up there less to clean the array. Bloody marvelous.There was a 3 month lead-time, but it was worth the wait, and instal day came with a team of half a dozen knowledgeable, friendly, professional people all raring to go from the moment they stepped foot on my property at 7am. They all knew what they were doing, worked well together, and i was happy to keep them in tea, and coffee, to keep their flow going, it was the least i could do.They finished the entire hardware installation in a single day, impressive for a large array like this, with Scott coming back the next morning for a few hours to show me the ropes for the software, etc. Then just had to wait for the inspection guy to come a few days later to give it the regulatory thumbs-up, before we could switch the system on and start enjoying our new house toy.The whole system is very well balanced, with the tilted panels collecting energy almost as soon as sun breaks in the morning, right until sunset at night, the battery is doing a fine job filling night-duty, sometimes completely lasting until sun-up next morning. Although that's great for the current summer, winter will reveal the bottlenecks for sure, and hopefully by then Tesla will have "vehicle to home" charging so we can add the Tesla car's 80KW battery to the house, saving us the need to buy more Powerwalls :)Overall my wife, and I, are beyond impressed with Jet Solar, really the antithesis to the trope of the "tradie/cowboy" company you always dread having to deal with.This is the kind of company that strives hard for their customer, and i'm the kind of customer that strives to make sure such companies get all the recognition they deserve :)To Adam, Scott, Jason, and the rest of the Jet Solar teams, a HUGE thank you from my wife, and I, here in Melbourne, and we look forward to recommending you to anyone who needs the best service, and value, for solar home installation !

Initially got a quote (and booked installation) for an Alpha Gen2 13.3kWh battery installed for $8990. WA rebate was to be $5000. Out of pocket $3990.Fast forward a couple of months, WA changed their rebate to $1300, but Federal Govt was also providing a rebate.2 weeks before install, their admin team sent a reminder of the install, what is to be installed, an invoice for the total amount (no rebate deducted) and a statement saying I had to pay it on the day on installation otherwise the battery wouldn't be activated.I reached out to PSW as I was under the impression the installer handled the rebate and it should come off the invoice total, plus there was no mention of the rebate changes or VPP for WA. Sales got back to me within a few hours, advising of the updated rebates, but also that the initial battery we had ordered was no longer available - huh? I just received an invoice stating I was being charged for it. How would this have played out if I never reached out asking about the rebate? They did say that if I wanted, I could get a "complementary upgrade" at "no additional cost" to a newer generation 15kWh battery - newer and larger upgrade for free!Turns out "complementary upgrade" at "no additional cost" is actually the cost increasing by $630; going from $8990 to $9620. But I guess in their eyes, as the rebate increased by $1620 ($1300 + $5320 vs $5000) due to a larger battery, there is no cost increase. Sure, my out of pocket hasn't increased, but the lure of a free upgrade at no cost increase, when there is a cost increase, just isn't right. Just say, "a newer battery with larger capacity will cost more, but you'll get more rebate back, so you won't be out of pocket any extra". Perhaps I'm being a little too pedantic on terminology? But words have meaning and the contracts they have you sign are very strict on the terminology used.My interactions with the company to date have been with sales staff and admin staff. Apart from the terminology/lures mentioned, the interactions with sales staff have been great. They were really prompt in getting back to me when I had questions.The admin staff, not so much. The first email they sent mentioned to reply if there were questions, but they never replied to questions; along with sending an invoice for a product they no longer had + failing to include rebates they are meant to administer...just felt lacking with the proficiency side of things. I had to do the prompting for rebate and VPP info, and then it was sales staff who answered. I would expect the admin staff to be all over those aspects of the business and be proactive with sharing information on it; some customers may not even beware of what questions to ask, but sadly the proactiveness is lacking.If you're not picky about those types of things, then you shouldn't have any problems.

System: 36 LG 370w panels, SME 10kw 3 phase inverter and a Powerwall2.  Not a typical installation!The PSW installation team was fantastic. Again, PSW was very good at delivering the best configuration possible.  It would appear that a 3 phase installation with a Powerwall is not that common in Perth (back in January).The system has worked flawlessly (except for a minor hiccup during a power outage, but this appears to have has been rectified), so I am very happy with the end solution and installation.  To date the system is performing better than my forecast; I have saved over $1050 in electricity costs in 6 months and expect a payback for the whole system in about 9 years.  Electricity bill for the 6 months was $80 inc. GST.  BTW, I get 0 cents credit from Western Power for input to the Grid, because I have a 10kwh inverter.  I would get whole 3 cents if I only had a 5kwh inverter.Things that weren’t obvious to me at the start, but is my fault for not investigating further:•	A single Powerwall can only support 1 phase.  2 Powerwalls can support 2 phases if configured that way, but only one works during a Grid outage.•	Western Power (via Tesla) limits the input/output of the Powerwall to 3kwh. This can impact the charge on very cloudy days.•	If the Grid goes down during the day, the Solar array stops as well because the inverter needs power to all 3 phases (the Powerwall only supports 1 phase).Would I recommend PSW?  Yes, definitely, but be prepared to do some fairly rigorous investigations yourself if you want a non-typical install (ie. not a 6kw solar only system).  I suspect this would be the case with most if not all installers.  I went with PSW because they provided a competitive price, quality service, were local and only used trained employees to do the installation.

We went with Solar Emporium for our solar panels, inverter and battery. Sales process was smooth.For context:We bought a house in a hilly green wedge area in Melbourne Australia.Eight weeks before we moved in  a massive storm came through and killed power to the house and neighbours. It was three weeks to a month before it was fixed.We went looking for solar/battery system quotes as soon as we moved in as both of us WFH. A series of faults and then nothing, just dead.We went through another round of seemingly hundreds of phone calls and finally got Sungrow to replace the battery as it was still under warranty. But Solar Emporium who should have organised the whole thing (Sungrow told us this) - they left it to us.To make matters worse, they left the old battery on site - a giant, possibly dangerous fire hazard item, in our carport, in a bushfire area, over summer - when part of the replacement works includes the battery being taken away for a post-mortem.So another round of calls and six months later (this is now almost two years in) they took the old battery away, we still had to organise paperwork for the courier.September 24 to 1 week ago: the replacement battery now has a fault - called Battery Management Systems fault where it cannot talk to the inverter and hence on a sunny day, the state of charge is zero. We've been calling Solar Emporium to send someone out to fix this as the fault will most likely lead to another dead battery, while we're having to pay for power.When you could get through to them, they make promises about "escalating you issue" and call you back then...nothing.We have tried calling, leaving reviews, facebook messages, instagram messages, no one EVER calls back, although everyone advises that the issue is being escalated.Last week till now:It has now escalated to another dead battery.Thoroughly disappointed, pretty angry to be honest, it's turning us into people we would rather not be.

One thing to consider before the installer arrives is what do you really want / need on the EPS circuit.  Getting the iSolarCould app to work correctly and recognise all of the equipment installed was challenging, but the installer persevered and after a 2nd site visit and several calls to Sungrow we had everything up and running. Happy Customer

I recently had solar panels and a Tesla Powerwall 3 installed at my home by JWS Electrical Services. The experience has been nothing short of outstanding. From the initial consultation to the final system activation, everything was handled professionally, efficiently, and with attention to detail.Josh took the time to analyse my energy usage, roof orientation, and long-term goals. He provided a clear breakdown of costs, savings, and how the Tesla Powerwall 3 would integrate into our daily energy use. I had my first rooftop solar system installed by JWS a few years ago. Reaching out for a quote I found their support staff to be extremely responsive, flexible and particularly knowledgeable - they know solar technology inside and out and can effortlessly discuss with you the merits and drawbacks of different systems, technologies and approaches. Conversely, they also don't harass you endlessly like many others do. I got the sense that they respected my time and weren't interested in bamboozling you into buying junk. Ultimately their quote was very competitive and their level of service and professionalism put them at the top of the list.The install was finished in a day and it's been going without a hitch, set and forget. After the install we had some heavy rain and I noticed a roof leak under where the panels were installed, I contacted JWS and they came out and spent the morning finding and fixing the leak. Hasn't been a problem since. I have had many professional services split hairs over emergent issues, spending more time and effort trying to defer responsibility than just fixing their work. JWS say they intend to leave your roof in a better condition than they found it, and my experience has suggested that is true.We moved house recently and so it seemed like a no-brainer to at least get another quote from JWS along with the 3 from SolarQuotes. The experience between the 3 SolarQuotes sent my way and JWS was night and day, and I was honestly surprised when JWS' quote was again very competitive. I honestly assumed at their level they'd be charging more, but I suppose the solar business must be pretty cutthroat.I had a lot of random questions about different technologies, brands and negotiating the new Federal battery rebate (before the election, risky!) and JWS were extremely patient and professional about it. In exchanges I had with other installers they seemed to rapidly get frustrated or veer off into making claims about brands and technology they were selling that simply could not be corroborated. JWS never struggled to make their case or substantiate their reasoning.Ultimately JWS became the clear choice again and everything was booked in quickly.Coincidentally, the day JWS came to install ended up being the day my wife gave birth to our second kid, and I could only be back and forth from the site very briefly, or take intermittent calls from them when I could. JWS' installers were very understanding of the situation and worked autonomously. They even identified a significant issue with our electrical connection to the grid, where we had a very out of date, underspecced connection to the powerlines that could have caused breakers to trip or become unsafe if overloaded. Even though I said clearly I did not expect them to fix it, they went out of their way to identify a solution and ensure the whole system was up to spec from end-to-end - for no additional cost.From start to finish JWS seems to be a well-managed outfit run by professional people, and I would happily recommend them to anyone. I replied to an online advertisement, which said that I would be contacted shortly; some weeks later, much longer than stated, I received a phone call from NSS. I am a forest-fire-fighter and the call was during a bushfire. I explained this and told them that it is usually difficult to contact me at work and could we communicate by email; the answer was no. Over the next few weeks, they rang me 2 or 3 times per week and eventually I managed to get them to ring my wife. A deal was agreed on and we deposited $3000 to get the process started.A few weeks later a man from Western Power arrived and changed the meter.About 10 weeks later, we contacted the person in charge of our case and left a message on her phone, asking what the progress was. There was no reply by later in the week, so my wife emailed her. The next day we received a bizarre email – strange that email was now an accepted form of communication. There was no greeting to either of us by name, just an announcement that our solar installation had been cancelled!…“At this current point in time we have had an issue with our installer who will no longer be representing Nationwide Solar Solutions. Given this issue we would be unable to move forward with your application and will have to cancel it. I understand that this is not the best option for yourself and our company, however given the time frame and lengthy delay I do not wish to waste anymore of your time and I am really sorry that it has taken this long for an update.”…Fair enough. Nice to know, but this is the strange bit:…“Please see the below list on solar installation companies that we have in WA and would recommend you liaise with for your future installation”….I don’t recall anything in the agreement, that said we had to work out the installation for ourselves!“…I understand that this is not the best option for yourself and our company, …”My wife and I agree with the NSS statement above.The only good news, was that we got our deposit back, after NSS had been earning interest on it for 10 weeks.No installation at all, back at square 1! Apparently NOT Nationwide; may be Solar; does not provide a Solution in WA.

After much research on solar batteries, quotes and confusion, we decided to go with Solaire Connect. Alex was on the ball right from the start and anytime we had a question, he would call. We wanted the battery to charge whilst there is a grid outage and for it to also have black start so it was zombie apocalypse proof. In a grid outage, the battery still runs our fridge and freezer, all lights, family room TV and power points for phones, our internet router so we still have Internet and our PCs should we need them.Price was very competitive and included everything with no hidden costs from start to finish. Already having a 5kw system that worked well, we wanted to expand the panels and install a battery to eliminate power bills as much as reasonably possible. The end result was the power generation is now great, the effectiveness of a very expensive 10kw Sonnen battery is dismal at best. The battery can supply only 4-6 hours of whole of house power, without using auxiliary units (IE: A/C, kettle etc) Given that the battery cost is $14K, it's ability to provide value for money does not exist, as it will require around 20+ years to pay for itself. This is a fact I was not aware of was anticipating it to be able to provide power for longer to the house once the sun goes down. It charges well and quickly from and efficiently place solar panels that capitalize well on our orientation, but the battery's ability to provide after sunset is very limited.I would have thought Solairre would have pointed out these limitations of the battery in our situation given they had a years worth of power bills, were fimiar with our current system working well, and should have been able to equate what we could reasonably expect from the battery. A  larger battery option should have been recommended and supplied.After installation was completed and a few days of operation was experienced with full sun days, we asked the salesperson to quote a bigger battery as we are sure the power generation is easily able to supply, to date we have not heard back from him.We will experience longer hours of generated power over the summer months of course, but the battery's ability to supply the house will not change.Are we disappointed with the installation? Yes, because the cost of the battery does not come close to representing any value for money whatsoever, however the new panels are working well.

I had some reservations about MyEnergy, for instance, the other 2 companies from which I had a quote attended personally, while MyEnergy was handled over the phone. However, their price was more competitive and it looked like their product was good quality (based on SolarQuotes YouTube videos). The government rebate differed in all three quotes (I investigated STCs!), but MyEnergy's rebate was higher. This seemed like a good sign that they passed on their STC value to the customer. Anyway, I got on very well with salesman Jawad and took the chance.Communication with the company was not the greatest and I had to chase up to get an installation date. Jawad, however, was always contactable and kept in touch and answered the several queries I had. Two days before that installation date I tried to get confirmation that it was happening (there'd been a lot of rain) to no avail. However, they turned up on the day as promised. The 22 panel installation was done in half a day, the battery, inverter and all electricals took the whole day.As for the grid connection, I was told by all companies that 'they would do the paperwork'. After installation, I decided to call my supplier (AGL) and check they were recognising the 'back to the grid' power. They hadn't been contacted by MyEnergy, but would set it up for me based on my call. A week later, after my full payment, MyEnergy sent me the 'paperwork' and advised me to contact my energy supplier. So, it appears, I had to do it after all. I called AGL, who advised me it was all set up and they didn't require that paperwork.The iSolarCloud app is giving me readings which appear odd sometimes, and I have sent in some queries to MyEnergy, and hope to get answers from them (they have confirmed receipt of my questions).Based on the cost, I think I have made the right decision (the next lowest quote was $7,000 more). The system design was based more on my budget than the other companies did.Top marks particularly to Jawad for his communication and attentiveness, before and after my signing up.

He tweaked the initial quote to increase the number of panels and decrease the size of the battery. We selected a suitable undercover space for the battery.At the day of installation 4 friendly & polite guys arrived: Matt, Luke, Simon and Jamo were a great team. The atmosphere between them felt good, an important one, as it makes you feel confident that there is a team that flows together and are confident with the job at hand. Since it was a sizeable job (14.48 kW in Aiko panels with a 24.18 kWh Sigengery battery) it took them 2 full days to set the system up. They gave good instructions at the end and left everything spotless. Thank you everyone at Great White Solar!

review_description: The salesperson was very knowledgeable, open and honest, understanding my needs rather than trying to sell a system. The quote was competitive. Recently contracted HOTT Electrics to augment our existing seven year old 4.9kW, Fronius/Trina installation. Their’s was one of four quotes obtained, and involved onsite inspection and discussion with the actual installer as opposed to remote/unseen estimates from the other three.  Answers to all our many questions with respect to this installation (including the complete upgrade of our old asbestos-backed switchboard which also became necessary) were readily provided and explained, as were system design suggestions/options to best suit our particular needs and situation.  All work was carried out by a very courteous, punctual, well-presented and totally professional crew, who were a credit to the business. There has also been prompt follow-ups in relation to metering and system performance.  The augmentation involved adding another separate string comprised of a Sungrow SH5.0RS hybrid inverter, Trina Vertex S+ 440w panels (1.76kW) with additional cabling for future expansion and a Sungrow SBR096 battery. Total system size now 6.66kW. Everything is working to specification and we are especially pleased with amount of visibility we now have of our power utilisation, that monitoring for all PV (both old and new) is handled efficiently by a single Sungrow app, having a backup capability and a future-proofed outcome.  Grid connection and all other grid-related issues were dealt with by the installer.P.S.  HOTT's belief in retaining and simply augmenting our existing system was an unprompted confirmation of a similar recommendation provided in prior exchanges we had with Anthony and Kim of SoarQuotes!

review_description: The service team at Yuma were fantastic, they took their time to explain the ins and outs of solar, what you should have and how it should be laid out on the roof...  compared to a major electricity supplier who looked on google maps and said you couldn't do it, Yuma took time to look at the orientation of the roof to get the maximum exposure and best price point...  The install team turned up promptly at 7:00am even though it had rained the night before, took us through the process, reconfirmed the proposed layout and made a suggestion to change the layout to suit the roof orientation even more... yes it was more work for them but the customer service experience was great... and no extra cost...  the electrician who connected everything up took his time to try and hide as much of the conduit as he could - nice and tidy job - one could say he was a bit of a perfectionist and took a lot of pride in his work, something you don't always see...  a follow-up call from Yuma after the install got the meter change over to a smart meter was timely but the changeover time was anything but timely... outside of Yuma's control and a reflection of the electricity supply industry... almost makes you want to install a power wall and go off grid...

True warranty horror story - Be afraid of these guysI purchased a 10k solar setup and tesla powerwall 2 7 to 8 years ago.Firstly they installed the solar 7 months later the battery.Big wait times.On install they damaged my roof tiles in 2 place cause water damage to the house.That cost me alot to fix.Nice !!The system worked well for about 2 years saving me a fortune before the battery packed it.They then removed it and I waited another 6 months for replacement.After this it worked well except that about once or twice a week (during summer) it would throw the earth leakage breaker causing all the power to go off.I was told you need to have an electrician look at it, not their problem.Which brings us to about a year ago when the battery stopped working altogether.After dealing with Solaray and now 1komma5, they don't even talk to you, you follow their lodge tickets online and eventually get shunted to a Phillipines call centre who can't help you.I was ignored time and time again.I contacted Tesla who say your installer needs to look at it.The installer call centre kept trying to make me run reboots and wifi setups for 6 months before I got Tesla to pressure them to sent a technician out.Even Tesla said we can see from our end that it's not working and they sent me screen shots of their data to send to the installer (who also has access to the same info already.)When the technician finally came out - he asked me why he was here. He was not even informed of the case progress and after several hours he said - everything is installed properly there's no issue,except your battery is not connecting.I'm like I've been telling you guys this for 1 year already.I said what happens next, he said we will put everything in the report to the installer.I have never heard from them again.They will not respond to emails or phone calls.These are the exact cowboys that will rip you off and not honour the warranty!Btw Tesla also will not honour the warranty - it needs to be done by your installer they say, even though their product is faulty/Stay away from both.PS - Solaray now 1komma5 was an installer recommended from this sites 3 quotes.I had tried to do all I could to pick the right ppl and right gear.Very disappointed - my last winter powerbill was $1250 even having 10k solar.I'm now faced with replacing the whole lot- lucky it has paid for itself 2 years ago.But now I should be enjoying 7 odd years of savings and I'm not!

The next week a second subcontractor came out and spent a morning trying to make the system work.Another week and SolarEdge advised the inverter needed to be replaced which would be  done under warranty. This was done by a third subcontractor and after 6 hours the system which had worked perfectly before the second battery was added was still no closer to working. What was more SolarEdge advised it was after the fact reneging on replacing the inverter under warranty.By now I’d have settled for returning the system back to the original as the installer and Solaredge didn’t seem to have a solution to fixing and neither seemed to want to fix the problem.I opened a SolarEdge case on their portal expressing extreme frustration. This was about 4 weeks after having no working system and getting charged higher electricity charges from the Amber wholesale market . No battery and I wasn’t shielded from price spikes.Another week and my case did jolt SolarEdge into doing something. It seems they sent out the wrong replacement inverter and now would replace it with a third under warranty.I’m still waiting for this third inverter to be delivered to the installer whereafter they have promised to come out and install and I hope restore the system. But my confidence in this being the outcome isn’t great but I’m really hoping it can’t get any worse…And to add salt into the wound, SolarEdge sent me the $500 cashback card which can’t be activated because it looks like it’s from some dodgy gift card company which can’t be contacted. This was a material inducement to why I invested in a second of their batteries.Overall to date a terrible experience.

The sales/quoting process was confusing. They were reluctant to do a site visit. I then found out they do not complete the installation but use a contractor. Arrived on time .Went through all the procedures straight away explaining where everything will be installed i.e battery placement ,cables and panels.Job completed on time and everything all setup and running by end of day.Very satisfied and so far have not encountered any faults.

Everything started fine - they met my price request, agreed to install in 1 week's time, turned up on time, then, in one day, they removed 2 old systems and installed 30 new panels, inverter and a Sungrow modular battery.  Since then, it's been all downhill from there.There was no commissioning of the system and no instruction of any kind other than to go online and find the iSolarCloud app. It turns out the inverter and the battery were wired incorrectly which, amongst other things, had excessive power being drawn from the grid and showed my house supplying power to the battery.  Also, after struggling to find, install and use the app without a user manual, I found that the app was faulty.1KOMMA5 answered my calls and emails and promised to look into the problems.  Twice they told me they had found a problem and were able to resolve it remotely but nothing had changed.  Their solution was to refer me to Sungrow to sort it out directly with them (which I refused).  After continually asking 1KOMMA5 for someone to come and check my system, they finally sent an Electrician one month after installation who discovered that the wiring had been totally botched and it took him most of the day to sort out.  This included selecting which circuits would be connected during backup mode which was not done originally.The sysyem now seems to be working properly as the power flows are going in the right directions and the grid usage is significantly lower.  However, it is now approaching 2 months since installation and I am still waiting to hear back about some issues with the battery performance and fixing the faults with the app.Of particular concern is that I have had to do all of the investigating to prove that specific problems existed with the system and with the app, and then spoon feed this research to 1KOMMA5 who have not shown any urgency to act.  I have given them 1 star for installation and for customer service only because this review process does not allow for a zero rating.

review_description: I recently had an 11 kW solar PV system with a 28.8 kWh battery installed by LECA, and I couldn’t be happier. The LECA sales people told us that the solar system 10kw plus with battery would "knock our power bill out of the park". We had it installed in January this year. We used to get bills in the preceding year of approx $700.00 now $500, however with the payback for the $15,000 loan for the system $120 per month we are in front about $80 (if we get fine weather), not really knocking the bill out of the park:( Coupled with the fact that we have had workman all over our roof and now have extra weight on the roof with solar panels and gods knows what else has been done and future maintenance cost and the Government future power bill increases, I believe we will be financially disadvantaged in the future:(As well the battery has not worked correctly since installation, apparently the brand new inverter is faulty and needs replacing. It has taken a lot of emails to finally get a new inverter delivered, however we are still waiting for someone from LECA to repair the system, apparently the installer who originally installed the system is sick and LECA tell me that other installers "by regulation" are not to work on other installers work, LECA did not quote the regulatory authority. LECA customer care tells me that someone will get back to me to arrange a repair date/time, but after a couple of weeks coupled with how long it has taken to get to this point I think I may have to wait another 6 months:(Additionally, because the battery system has not worked, I have been trying to get financially compensated for the lost money. It is now near November, I have been offered only $250.00, with know clear explanation how they worked out how much money they owe us. LECA says that they only pay from the date the fault was formally reported to when the new inverter is delivered, not satisfactory in my book:(The ACT Government should be ashamed for getting into business with the residential solar power companies. They have legitimised the validity of these companies:( As you usual the consumer has to pay and pay and pay and pay !!!!!!! Reviewing the cost of the system, I calculated it should of been $16,943, but LECA put it as $26,442.50, I was told to ignore this on the paper as it was so we could get the $15,000 interest free loan from the ACT Government. In the end the full cost was $17,300, we had to pay $2,300.00 for the difference between $15,000 loan and total cost $17,300. We were supposed to get off the total cost the STC Incentive $4,968 and NEXT GEN Grant $4,174, however that money seemed to evaporate perhaps LECA could explain:(

Installation went ahead with a very friendly and professional crew who kept us fully informed all the way through. They were a well oiled machine! Since installation Heaps Good have kept in contact checking in and filling us in on how the system is working and what we thought and think.We cannot recommend Heaps Good Solar highly enough. But hey, at least they can say they went around & tried, right?Oh, & then I get the bill and some pressure to pay - while they've charged me for concrete sheeting that they never installed. Managed to get that forted at least - by simply not paying. Then, frankly, my stress levels with this company just became too much & I want them out of my life.So all in all, I have an ap which gives me about 40% of the information I would expect to be able to access about my battery. The quoting process with Sunterra and Graham was by far the best and most responsive of all the quotes we received. He was amazing at making sure all my questions were answered and seemed knowledgeable and very helpful.Unfortunately the next stage of the process was where the Sunterra let themselves down. July 2023 was when we first approached Sunterra and finally agreed in September 2023. Things progressed quickly then an install date was set with a third party contractor. We have a steep colorbond roof with multiple sections (35 degrees to which some people wouldn't even install on) and I think this played a part in the issues.- 1st install attempt - weather delay as it was raining. The problem was they didn't tell me this until after midday when they were due at 7am.- 2nd install attempt - weeks later - excuse made by 3rd party contractor but refused to reschedule. 2 more weeks went by with no contact whatsoever. I threatened to pull the pin on the job. Was then asked if 'there was a way to get panels onto my roof?' A question I was shocked by.Another week went by before an in house installer came to measure and review (the first time anyone had actually been to the house). Eventually a plan was made a month or so after the original installation date with their in house installers.The 3rd party installers were unreliable and never turned up once. Do not use their 3rd party installers if you can avoid it.Final installation date was agreed in mid November 2023. Zac was great and the 2 day install went pretty smoothly. We found out later that the staging part of my roof (a flatter walkway covered section) was damaged by the installers not walking on the rivets. Hence the 'pretty smoothly'.We discussed several options for the wiring and backup circuits and implemented them. Ended up with almost all power circuits connected to the EPS which is great but it turns out you can't keep the EPS switch on all the time with a Microwave connected as there is an amp limit running through the battery. A slight inconvenience but overall not a deal breaker. SO we run with Grid mode on, meaning if the power goes out we have to switch back on or deal with the microwave cutting off the EPS randomly while we have full grid power available.After installation all of the connections, inspection and paper work was done really quickly (within a week) and we were away. Great customer service from that perspective.Then we found the damage, 7-8 sheets of colorbond was dinted and folded. Customer service eventually organised 2 tradies through Hi Pages to quote. This process was almost entirely managed by us. They had no idea what the job was when they rocked up. Overall it all got fixed, but the guy that ended up doing it tried to tell me they don't make my colour sheets any more so he got the 'closest too it' but he clearly got the colour wrong. Couldn't be bothered changing and arguing so left it at that. This colour difference was no fault of Sunterra, but they could at least have trusted local tradies they use, not randoms off Hi Pages.Overall Sunterra did a good job, were let down by some contractors and silly mistakes but I am happy with the system working as it should.Would I recommend them, I would, but you need to be switched on to manage the process.

review_description: Had KIK Electrics recommended through this site. Went with them despite being more expensive than I'd hoped - had found cheaper services previously didn't really have super outcomes so hoped if I spent a bit more this time I might be better off. Absolutely no problems with the system as far as I can tell - seems to be working really well and we are not drawing from the grid at all. Problem is, we can't feed into the grid because KIK have not sent on the proper documentation to the energy provider. This means that we can't provide any excess energy produced into the grid and our system shuts down if production exceeds use and the battery is already full, which is a massive waste. Company won't reply to me now - massive red flag!!! I have also found out that our VicSolar loan has not been able to commence because they haven't sent the paperwork to them either, so something seems to be going wrong at that end of the business. Will be interesting to see if I can ever get this system feeding into the grid and how it will operate when at full capacity. At the moment, although a 11+kW system, I have never had it produce more than around 4kW at any time, as I can't export the excess. So, fair to say my experience with them has not been great. Having said this, their installation was fast and tidy, so nothing wrong with that side of things.

Two installers recommended by SolarQuotes were very punctual and close on prices quoted (the third was very slow). However, I selected KIK electrics who were not on the list provided by SolarQuotes but were on their list of reviewed installers. KIK electrics consistently had high scores (4-5) from reviewers and, importantly, zero poor reviews. A poor review can be 'flushed away' by an adequate installer response, but otherwise they just sit there and contaminate a lot of otherwise good work.One of two directors of KIK electrics, Justin, answered my phone call and was immediately on top of my requirements. Their quote was similar to the earlier two, and Justin made helpful suggestions about a modular BYD battery, and waiting to collect data from the Fronius inverter to see if we really needed to spend more on another module for the battery.The installation team of four arrived at 8am on the appointed day and worked till 6pm in 30+ degrees to get the job completed. Justin arrived the next morning to set up the monitoring system and install a (free) range extender. Justin also organised all of the grid connection details and has been happy to answer a few follow-up queries.

Overall l was very impressed with the service from KIK Electrics and have already recommended them to friends.
