I purchased a solar system consisting of 51 x trina panels, 2 x Sungrow 10kw 3 phase hybrid inverters and 2 x Sungrow batteries each consisting of 4 x 3.2kw modules from Arkana in January 2023 on the basis of the representations made to me that doing so would reduce my electricity bill by approximately 92%. At the time of purchase I questioned the cost of the Sungrow battery modules which were well in excess of the prices listed by Solarquotes. I was told in writing that the information on your site was incorrect and that Arkana had as a result had Sungrow amend their advertised prices.While Arkana was responsive at the stage of sale and installation, their performance after installation was poor. First I had a problem with the communication between the Sungrow equipment and the phone app downloaded to monitor performance. Arkana initially told be that the problem was with my wi-fi coverage and that I needed to upgrade that at my own expense. I spent more than $500 doing so with no improvement in the system communication. Eventually almost 2 months after the initial installation their technician attended my property and installed a sun cover over the externally mounted inverter and communications dongles on the two inverters which solved the problem.Next I discovered that the reduction in my power bill was nothing like what Arkana had suggested it should be. When I raised the matter with them I was told that the problem was that I had a very large property and high electricity usage, but that their system was generating the amount of power they said it would. That was not the point and I have since worked out for myself that the real problem was that they had recommended and installed insufficient battery capacity given my use profile.Next I asked them to quote for the installation of additional battery modules. Ultimately they quoted me an instqlled price inclusive of GST  of almost $3000 per module for each additional 3.2kw Sungrow battery module. When I suggested that that price did not seem competitive and that I would approach alternate solar Installers for quotes, Arkana’s initial response to me was that if their installation was touched by another solar company they could not continue to warrant their work. Not surprisingly I took issue with that,  and approached an alternate supplier.In percentage terms Arkanas price was 259% of what I paid.In addition when the new company installed the additional modules they discovered that the export limit for my system which should have been set at 15kw—5kw per phase—had been incorrectly set at  10kw total which means that in the 6 months between the Arkana installation and the upgrade my export credits should have been 50% greater.Not only were my credits less than they ought to have been it is pretty clear that I paid Arkana far more than I should have been charged for their installation looking at the exorbitant quote provided to me for the battery upgrade.I would clearly advise potential customers to avoid Arkana.

We recently engaged SOLARLAB in Adelaide to install our new solar system.  The final system design ended up with 22 Hyundai 390W shingled panels and Enphase IQ7+ microinverters, the Envoy-S along with a Telsa PowerWall.We don't have a north facing roof, and some of our panels had to face east (approx azimuth 131 degrees), bulk of them to the west (approx azimuth 312 degrees), and a little bit of shading in the late afternoon on some of the west facing panels.  We all agreed that the micro inverter option would most likely provide us with the best result, along with our desire to avoid the high voltage DC in the roof from a string setup.  To support the bulk of the electrical loads in the house from a blackout and provide possible future support for an electric vehicle, we also went ahead with a Tesla PowerWall battery unit.The whole engagement, from the first sales visit, right through to the installation and commissioning of the system was great.  All of the SOLARLAB staff were very friendly and nothing was too much trouble.  There were no pushy sales tactics, and they were willing to discuss different designs and what the benefits of each were.  Most other companies just seemed to install a simple string setup to keep the price down, maybe thinking the lowest price wins.Once the install was finished, a small issue with the Envoy-S incorrectly limiting the exported power was resolved quickly without any fuss or drama.  At one time or another we spoke with everyone from the CEO through to the guys fixing the racking and panels to the roof, everyone was great to work with.One of the things that we really liked about SOLARLAB is that they have their own people to do all of the work, they don't contract the work out to other companies.  We think this gives a more consistent result on the installations and the care that goes into the job certainly shows.We are really happy with the finished system, and considering the alignment of the panels because of our roof layout, the system still generates an impressive amount of power.  On most days so far, we have not had to draw any power from the grid (other than the few really hot days in Feb when we had to run our A/C, which is a big unit) and have exported anything up to 42kWh of power to the grid, after charging the PowerWall up and satisfying the needs of the house during the day.  The PowerWall typically discharges down to around 83% capacity overnight after running a TV, the fridge, some inside lighting (now all LED) and a porch light at the front of the house.  It is normally fully charged by 10:30am and ready to go for the next night's requirements.SOLARLAB organised all of the approvals, assisted with a "green" finance package with one of their partners, guided us through the Home Battery scheme sign up that we have here in SA which provides a State Government backed subsidy for home battery storage and even booked the smart meter replacement with our electricity retailer.As with any solar system, to get the best of it you need to adjust when you use most of your electricity.  The SolarQuotes team has provided advice on this on the website, and it is amazing what a few small changes to your consumption habits can make.  After only a few weeks from the installation and by using the stats from the Tesla and Enphase apps it has been really easy to make these small changes.If you are located in South Australia, we would highly recommend including SOLARLAB on your list of companies to talk to about a solar system.

Having access to both the Telsa app and Enphase app has been fantastic to be able to see both a system summary and panel-by-panel performance insight.Lucas was really helpful during the whole process and the installation team where kind and considerate. The whole process started off ok, with the sales person being quite helpful, albeit quite pushy and pressuring me to place an order straight away once the quote was received. I had a phone call on 27/2/24 stating the installation would commence the next day. Short notice I thought, but was happy to at least get things started. However on double checking that the install included solar panels, battery and HWS I was told that the company was having trouble sourcing the HWS and that would be done at a later date. As the installation of the solar panels necessitated the removal of our existing solar HWS from the roof I told the caller that everything needed to be installed at the same time otherwise we would be without hot water until the new HWS was received and installed. He seemed surprised at this and said he would check again with the supplier. Another phone call 4 hours later informed me they had sourced a HWS and would be starting installation on 4 March 2024.  The installation process took 3 days with 3 electricians not arriving until 11am each day. An apprentice put his foot through our ceiling while in the roof space which will cost over $1,700 to repair. (this amount was deducted from our payment to Sungain) The installers also cut through the roof sarking during installation and when I queried why this happened I was told that was the only way to do it and that the sarking would be repaired before the colourbond roof panel was replaced. On checking this the next day the sarking had NOT been repaired and the roof panel had been replaced. The sarking was eventually repaired. The HWS was EXTREMELY heavy and had apparently been loaded onto the installers truck with a forklift (it was on a pallet) However NO thought was given as to how it would be unloaded with no lifting equipment available at our address. It took 3 electricians, 1 plumber and 2 of us to get it off the truck and into position and it was a miracle the unit wasn't damaged in the process. The HWS seems to be working well so far. I have some queries about the output of the solar panels as the mobile app shows that the panels are only producing up to around 450w at any given time? I would have thought such a large system would produce more than that? The app also shows that the battery is fully charged but when usage in the household increases or when the sun has gone down there is no power coming from the battery into the house, it all seems to be coming from the grid which to my mind defeats the purpose of having a system with a battery? All in all the whole process has been unprofessional and very frustrating. I would definitely not recommend Sungain to anyone considering purchasing a solar system

I didn’t go for the cheapest quote, because I believe you get what you pay for. I wanted honestly and reliability. It is a big investment and and I wanted quality products and a reliable installation. I’ve already received post installation assistance.

Daniel from B & L Electrics was absolutely brilliant with my 24kW Sigenergy battery install. His service was outstanding — personable, attentive, and incredibly helpful from start to finish. He beat all other quotes, left the site spotless, and made the whole process a pleasure. Couldn’t be happier with the experience — extremely highly recommended!I am so glad I chose this company!

My roof was very complex and required a bespoke design, especially to maximise the number of solar panels that could be installed in accordance with the standards. It was also a difficult roof to work on safely.Daniel Slade is the owner of B&L Electrics (and an experienced and qualified electrician who has been doing solar installations for a number of years).He would not do a quote without a thorough roof and property inspection, which I considered a necessity to ensure that the price reflected the complexity and quality of the final installation that I required.The on site inspection also allowed me to discuss the project with Daniel to assess both the likely quality of the finished design and installation and also how I could work with Daniel. As I have a lengthy construction background, the quality and job safety were paramount to me.Daniel also has a young apprentice (Chris). It was a delight to have both Daniel and Chris work on my installation and the level of safety concern was superb. Especially Daniel’s concern for Chris.Communication with Daniel was excellent! He and Chris were reliable, courteous and always cleaned up at the end of the day.Care was taken with the selecting excellent quality equipment, materials and fittings. And the design delivered me more panels than others had suggested. And many others would not quote because the roof was of a somewhat complex shape.I had no issues or problems with Daniel, Chris or with their installation. Daniel did not encounter any unexpected or unplanned difficulties so there was no question of variations or cutting corners with the work to meet the price.After nearly 2 full weeks of use of the solar system I am very happy with its performance and the monitoring that I am able to easily do. And that is despite most of the time since the installation was completed, being rather cloudy and wet.I give my highest recommendation to Daniel and Chris for the total project, from the initial site visit to the final clean up, handover and commissioning of the solar system. (A Sungrow battery will be installed in a few months when the maximum cost reduction becomes available from both the state and federal governments. And the wiring for an EV charger has also been installed ready for an EV charger when the need arises.)If you choose Daniel and Chris you will get a great team and a superb quality solar installation.

Installation was efficient, Daniel and Chris turned up on time and did the install in a very timely manner.Daniel spent some time with me to explain how things worked, safety features and the likeThey left the place spotless, inside and out.There was a problem with the app on my phone, but that was solved by a reinstall of the app

Hi FinnWhilst I did not go with one of the suppliers you had contact me, I can say that without your Website and the tremendous amount of quality information it contained, the journey I travelled towards the installation of Solar Power would have taken much longer. After further investigation I have had an 8Kw system installed with LG 335W panels and a Solaredge 8Kw Inverter and Optimisers. I apologise for not getting back to you sooner

I appreciate all the information you provided me. I used it  to make comparisons between the range of products and services offered by two of your recommended suppliers and two others I researched about. The knowledge on your website gave me confidence in making the right decision, which was not just based on price.

The salesperson was quick to contact me (reached out on the same day I submitted my inquiry through Solar Quotes). Over the course of the next two weeks, they were in contact often. It was slightly overbearing at times but they were able to meet my budget constraints and I was happy with the quote, so we signed and went head.Installation was scheduled for a week and a half later. There were a team of four there bright and early. It took two days from start to finish. The end result was very processional. Cables managed well around the inverter and switchboard, and panels positioned to take advantage of the sun direction.Everyone I spoke to was professional and clearly both knew what they were doing, and were passionate about it. If I was really being picky, the only thing that perhaps could have been a little better was communication in the time before and after the installation. There were a few days after signing where I didn't know what was happening, and after the installation working out what needed to be done for feed-in to be activated, but I fully understand this is due to it being a very busy period.I wouldn't hesitate to recommend GreenSaver Solar to friends and family in the future!

The sales process was a bit clunky.  They originally provided me with a few options/estimates which I found a little confusing before sending around their specialist to do a site inspection and provide a guaranteed quote.  During the site inspection the specialist was the only one who actually got up on my roof, listened to my concerns about string vs optimised panels and provided some good advice on how to use the system once it was up and running.The installers were lovely and polite, arrived on time on both days and left the outside clean and tidy at the end of both days of the install.  The finished job with the battery and inverter looks lovely and neat.

The Sales / Quoting process from Helcro Solar was great.  They responded to my queries and requests for tweaks with prompt responses and came up with the best value for money quote.The installer, I think, was a subcontractor to Helco and was neat and competent.  However, I was asked to pay a further $1000 by the installer to make my switchboard fully compliant despite the accepted quotation including $1050 for Partial Blackout Protection circuits and compliant componentry.  I feel I am being over charged for a couple of breakers here and this should have been included in the original scope of works.The old decommissioned solar system and pile of packaging from the new system was left in my driveway for a week and was only removed when I followed it up with Helcro.  I think this was another oversight by the subcontract installer.The Independent Inspector came 3 days after the installation on a Saturday morning and was quick and pleasant to deal with.  The system was put into service and is working perfectly.  One query I had with the Inspector related to the installation of a smoke detector above the battery as this was not done by the installer.  He explained that technically this was not a "shall" be installed but just a "should" be installed requirement and suggested I get one from Bunnings myself.The panels have been installed as designed but some seem to be sitting a little bit out of plane alignment.To date there has been no explanation of the System.  The MySigen phone App is easy enough to understand but a better understanding of the System and Gateway would be helpful.

Once signedn, HelcroSolar was responsive to any request which was impressive given the increased business associated with the opening of the Federal rebate. The process was fully described with HelcroSolar facilitating paperwork and keeping us appraised of timeliness.

The process from getting a quote till installation went really smoothly and ease. They were very effective in communication and gave detailed report/information about the various options for battery, panels, inverter. The people who came to install were very helpful and friendly - they explained and left instructions how to use the battery, inverter and even the switch board. Everything was really clear, transparent and detailed. I was really impressed at their ability, performance and quality service they provided for us.

The Helcro Solar sales process was the best I experienced out of 6 installers who quoted me. Marian spent considerable time explaining the advantages of different systems using clear language and also sent emails summarising the phone discussions. They were the only installer who offered to send someone on site rather than just quote through the software.The quoted price was a little higher than some other installers however I believe you get what you pay for - lowest price is not always the best. The installers arrived on schedule and were quite unobtrusive whilst working. They removed all the rubbish at the end of the job and fixed all the roof tiles that were broken. They also fixed a minor electrical fault that arose on the second day.The administration of the project was all done promptly and correctly by the Helcro Office, including emails explaining the entire process.

Helcro’s recently installed a 6.6kW Solar System and a 10kw battery in my house. The experience I have with Helcro has been fabulous, from the beginning of seeking for quotes to the application of rebates and installations.I sought for a number of quotes from different companies, but Helcro win my complete trust in advising me the best product that suit my needs and budget, and that they will do the best job with the installation. Marian, the sale manager at Helcro is amazing. She is knowledgeable, responsive, professional and friendly. She gives me full attention and understanding my needs before responding. Before finalising the quote, an electrician also came to my house and climbed to the roof to inspect (which I greatly appreciated). Upon accepting the quote, Helcro processed the SolarVic rebate within 24 hours. The operation team and Jenny are very responsive in keeping us posted with the installation schedule. The installation took 3 days. On the third day, someone at the Government (Energy Safe Vic) came to do a compliance check before the solar system is commissioned. Shout out to the installation team and the electrician (Bradley)!!! They are very professional and respectful. They communicate clearly and transparently. They give me an update of the installation progress at the end of each day. The installation only finished yesterday and I am very pleased with this process so far!Overall, I highly recommend Helcro. I get what I pay for and I have faith in Helcro’s capability to do the best installation.

Sales/quoting process.Extremely patient, knowledgeable and supportive staff who was able to answer my many questions. He was also very helpful in sourcing the products that we preferred.InstallationInstallation team was punctual and polite. Installation went smoothly abate the change of dates due to staff illness and inclement weather. Safety procedures were strictly adhered to all the time.Customer serviceTen out of ten. We had numerous questions post-installation. They were answered by the appropriate staff and we also had a visit from one of the co-owners. He went through the emergency procedures with us again and explained the functions of the various switches in the switchboard.Overall, we are very impressed with the services provided by the whole team, from the initial site assessment to the post-installation visit.Highly recommend their services.

Helcro Solar was the slowest and most expensive of 3 quotes I received from SolarQuotes.  I chose Helcro because its staff and team appeared to be most knowledgeable of the trade and most professional.  I do not regret my decision.Sales person was thorough and patient with my questions.   He provided with sound advice  and rationales why Goodwe was chosen.  He was knowledgable about potential issues with other products, which I verified independently.An electrician was attended a site visit with detailed photos and videos recording the condition of my roof, switchboard, and discussed potential location for battery.  Orientation of PV panels were justified.  He also explained some of the issues that I may not have been aware of.  Eg only part of the house will be connected to battery so to conserve battery in case of extended power outage without great impact on the running of the house.  We also discussed why I would not benefit from a bigger system, which I was skeptic for a while.  Now I see Helcro provided an excellent advice especially after learning about export limits and my actually power consumption.Excellent communication from Helcro with prompt follow up on my solar applications.  Installation team was on time, in fact early, which is rare amongst tradies.  Work site was nearly maintained.  I can only assume installation was done with care.We had some issue connecting the battery.  The operation team acted on it almost immediately.   A second person came in to have the problem rectified.Unlike some of the installers, customer services become poor post installation, Helcro has been excellent with customer services post installation.  I was ignorant with export limits and a few other issues.  Helcro responded to my queries promptly, on numerous occasions.

Right from the very start, service was excellent. Ben came around for a site inspection, which was very useful. Other installers just quoted based on aerial photographs, which didn't pick up the shading issues from neighboring buildings. Helcro was very quick to provide the quote after the site inspection (I don't think Shuey ever sleeps, he would reply to emails at all hours!).The installers were on time and clearly knew their stuff. The installation is neat and tidy, and everyone was very friendly. Can't fault the process or the overall experience. Would definitely recommend!

I had Helcro Solar install a solar system at my home, and I couldn't be happier with my purchasing experience. The Helcro team got to outcome of a new solar system for my property. There were challenges on the way but eventually all is working well.

Sales/ quoting was excellent. Helcro listened to my requirements in both price and equipment and came up with an appropriate installation. I am delighted to write a positive review for Helcro Solar and their contractor, Andrew (Chispa Electrical). Thank you, Helcro Solar and Andrew, for your excellent work!

I felt like I was buying a quality system, not just the cheapest, The install went very smoothly and professionally. Great customer service. I feel I can approach Helcro long after the install date. Still waiting for the grid feed in tariff to be established.

The three quotes came in quickly but only one company insisted on a site visit, the other two declined saying it wasn't necessary. Because I was replacing an older 3kW PV only system with a larger system + battery I would only deal with a company that would do a site visit. As it happened Helcro was the most realistic with their assessment pricing was competitive (mid range of the 3) and they communicated with good technical information not a hard sales push. I also chose Helcro also because they used Lithium iron phosphate batteries and for safety and ethical reasons I didn't want cobalt in the battery. Having had solar I had a good idea of the usage pattern and upgraded their suggested battery size by adding an extra module to the BYD battery. Installation process was seamless and everything clicked in after the inspection. However, one month later the system dropped off the app. Turned out it was not a technical hitch with the inverter communicating with the app but a stuff up in the paper work with the energy supplier. Got that sorted and Helcro responded quickly, so now all is forgiven and the system is working brilliantly. Even in the middle of a Melbourne winter there are many days when we don't draw anything from the grid.

Scott, Kristi-Lee and the team at PSD were fantastic to deal with. Very professional work, great attention to detail and completely reliable and contactable. Would use any time without hesitation. Sorted everything for the Tesla powerwall, solar panels and connections.

Awesome group of staffBest customer serviceThe best people to have your solar installed by they are reliable, prompt ,very clean and extremely beautiful  bunch off people to have at your place doing the work.The electriction they have on the job is the best .Can't recommend this company enough  Thank you Thank you Platinum Solar .

Stay far away from Think Renewable. This has been a train wreck of experience, leaving us with a $20k bill, and no working system. We will be chasing this up with the ACCC, and looking into further legal advice from this point forward, if necessary.Short Abstract: “We purchased a $20k solar system with battery backup. The Alpha ESS inverter/battery was displaying multiple errors immediately post installation and system was not working on the same day it was installed. There is a very real possibility that we were lied to about the functionality of the system, in order to get us to sign off on the installation.Upon chasing this up with Think Renewable, they have washed their hands of any responsibility, and stated it’s a warranty issue that the battery company with have to deal with it. This has left us without any power on Saturday, and system that doesn’t work. It’s been left to us to chase up getting it fixed/the new parts installed when the parts are eventually shipped out to us by the battery company.”Full version:The initial experience with the sales consultant was positive. It was an easy and simple process. We ordered a 10KW solar system with an Alpha ESS battery backup for $20,000. This is where the good experience ended. During the installation (on a Wednesday), the installers had issues getting the system working properly. Once they managed to “resolve the issue”, the installers stated that “a fault light on the battery system was normal until it goes into backup mode with a power outage”. They got me to go inside while they “turned the power off” to verify it was working correctly. At this point I had no reason to doubt them, and signed off on the installation as I was pushed to do. In hindsight, it’s unclear if the power was even turned off for the test.It was 2 hours later that I went outside to check on the alpha ESS system to find that the solar was not generating electricity, and the battery system was displaying multiple  low temperature errors (we are in Perth and it was 30°). Their business was closed, so I called at the open of business the next morning to raise the issue (Thursday morning). We were told that the tech specialist would be in contact shortly. We never heard back from the tech specialist after multiple points of contact. After numerous phone calls, we were told that the complaint has been passed off to Alpha ESS (the battery supplier) to rectify; as there is a verified issue. They had no interest in sending a tech out to look at it, and that “we are waiting for Alpha ESS to get back to us”. We were told that if we don’t hear back by Monday, to try calling them again.Fast forward to Saturday, we lose all power to our house and the Alpha ESS battery system is going haywire. The screen on the unit is flickering and we can’t get power back. It is the weekend and there are no emergency contacts to be had. We finally managed to get ahold of someone over east and they contacted the WA branch for us. Think renewable, once again, didn’t feel it necessary to send a tech out, and a member of the WA team instead walked us through a restart procedure. This didn’t work, and after hours of trying to rectify, we managed to get the power back by doing a restart procedure, but leaving the built in isolator switch for the inverter turned off. In other words, our inverter blew!Think Renewable said they would chase this up with Alpha ESS; as this is a warranty issue. Alpha ESS would send the parts via post, and when we receive them in the mail, to call and book an installation. This is where we began to become further suspect that we were lied to about our system functioning at installation. That way Think Renewable wouldn’t have to rectify this issue, the battery supplier would.It is now Wednesday (a week post install). We still don’t have a working system, and replacement parts haven’t even been shipped by Alpha ESS. When the parts do finally arrived it’s up to us to book installation of the new components.This isn’t good enough

Ltd. I evaluated many facets of the quote and formed a short list. They were at the top and I accepted their reasonable quote.They are a known quantity and they worked with me in getting this unique challenge on our roof.In having our kitchen renovated with floor to ceiling cupboards and pantrys, I neglected having any thought about the existing panels on the roof above the range hood.That was a bad oversight on my part and I took ownership of my error and I worked towards rectifying it in the easiest logical way to allow the range hood exhaust tube exit upwards through the tiled roof and allowing our TV antenna to stay.I consulted with Mo, the owner & head installation guy, I ran the idea past him and he agreed it can be done.As we have used his services before with regards to 50 panels being installed a few years ago, it was actually a no brainer. Price does not reflect quality of workmanship. You get what you pay for.I watched Mo work and was very impressed with his careful and concise work ethic. My own forté is Electronics, design and repair/ service so an appreciation of good workmanship was indeed absolutely paramount.The installation date was set for Monday 28th June 2021 at 7:30 am and they arrived on time.While his crew were in the process of carefully removing the existing 22 x 275 watt panels, his guys showed me many broken tiles that were broken installed by a previous solar panel company. That, sadly was so very obvious.We have had water leaks in our lounge room, paint falling off etc. for quite a few years, but could not exactly see why. The broken tiles were under the 275 watt panels and revealed as each panel was lifted.Anyhow, the 22 plus 2 spare 275 watt panels were moved and carefully mounted very well. A work of art and as well as a whirly gig roof ventilator moved to accommodate the moved, now 24 275 watt panels.Based on the information about the quantity of broken tiles, we had to ring around and source 35 CLARK cement tiles of the WINDSOR style.Come next day, Tuesday 29th June, my wife and I drove to Prospect very early  to buy 35 tiles and bring them back in time for Mo, Richard and Yousuf to do their thing.It helps to know your panel installer was once a tiler earlier in his work life. He carefully fitted the replacement tiles. Well done indeed Richard.The final 17 x 390 watt matt black panels were installed by about 2:30 pm, rain halted things for a half hour, then back into it.Mo had installed the Fronius 3 phase inverter and was completing the wiring carefully. By 3pm it was just about done and dusted. Mo went around and checked everything. He took his time to go over each and every connection before he could commission  the installation. At about 3:20pm he was satisfied all was well and went about switching it all on, all 91 solar panels and three inverters and one existing SONNEN 15 KWatt battery that Mo and his Green Solar Energy had installed a few years earlier and had been working well since it was commissioned back then.Despite being a cloudy afternoon, at 3:45pm, the installation was generating 13.7Kwatts. I cannot wait to see how it all runs in summer.Outstanding job. Awesome results.I have the greatest pleasure in recommending Green Solar Energy Pty Ltd, fantastic service, great price and a job exceptionally well done.Prompt, courteous, polite and cleaned up all mess. The broken tiles were removed also.Jeff & Vickie

Okay I’m revising my original review of Stag Electrical. The reason is while my angry rant made me feel better it wasn’t particularly helpful to others. I now recognise Stag was incredibly naive and unrealistically complacent rather than necessarily incompetent. And I have to accept that more assiduous work on my part may have helped to avoid the shambles this became.Just a recap: I sought quotes through SolarQuotes near the end of April 2025, and received 3 referrals. I ordered a Powerwall 2 and paid the deposit to Stag Electrical in early May. This was to be the second Powerwall for my system. No other battery (including other Tesla batteries) was compatible. If I failed to secure a Powerwall 2 then I was stuck with a substandard solution for the foreseeable future. Tesla ceased production of Powerwall 2s in 2024 and old stock was rapidly disappearing. On top of that the federal government had introduced the battery rebate! And in Canberra there were rumours that the government interest-free solar loans were going to cease on 30 June (which in fact did occur); while I wasn’t getting a loan this promoted even more demand for batteries. This was the proverbial perfect storm and to say it made me nervous is an understatement.I contacted all who quoted and expressed my concerns about my fear of Powerwall 2s disappearing in the frenetic buildup to the start of the federal battery rebate. They agreed with me and said they would bring  a Powerwall 2 into their stock as soon as I paid the deposit. One reason I am modifying my review is that I can’t recall Stag Electrical making that specific undertaking. I had assumed anyone who worked in the industry as long as Stag would do the same as other suppliers and physically secure the stock. But I don’t recall explicitly asking for this. My bad number one.I still think Stag could have, with minimal effort, secured a Powerwall 2 battery rather than rely on reserving one with a wholesaler who was obviously going to be under immense pressure to satisfy an unprecedented demand for stock to desperate installers. Just about everyone in the industry had predicted this. And Powerwall 2s were special in my case because I could not expand my system with any other battery.The second area where Stag let me down was implying my Powerwall was available in each of my follow-up phone calls. They were even offering assurances to me in June, although apparently now saying they found out (in July admittedly) that Powerwall 2s ceased to be available in May. I accepted those undertakings, again based on my previous dealings with Stag and SolarQuotes endorsement of them. My bad number 2.So on 1 July I was waiting for the call from Stag to tell me when my installation would occur. The call I got on 14 July was that Stag could not source a Powerwall 2 even though they had been trying for the past 2 weeks. I was not a happy camper to find out that not only had they not secured stock but had also been giving me assurances for the past 2 months that everything was on track. I may have overreacted a little.While the result was initially devastating for me, I have to concede that I could have been more explicit and rigorous in keeping Stag on track, and have to accept that.I still think Stag should have, as an experienced operator in the industry, done more to secure a battery without the need for a customer to constantly hassle them. But lessons learned.Just because an installer has provided good service in the past there is no guarantee they will continue to do so.SolarQuotes endorsement of an installer is a low bar and due diligence requires much more than relying on that.

Troy rang Ergon as there is high voltage & have organised for Ergon to fix the problem.The boys did not mind my dog Moe watching them.I could not have asked for a better crew they were fantastic & all very polite & knew what they were all doing. A special thank you to Troy & Dylan
company_name: Hielscher Electrical and Communications Pty Ltd

review_description: Brenton was very informative and helpful in relaying what the system was about and how it all worked.The office staff (Carolyn) were very polite and helpful as well.Early days after the install but going by the systems performance so far, it's looking very positive for the future.
company_name: Hielscher Electrical and Communications Pty Ltd

review_description: Fantastic installation team. Beautiful install, so neat and tidy. The design is off grid and incorporates both AC and DC coupled equipment. So happy I'd love to try and power my neighbours hose as well!The owner incorporated much of my small scale DC coupled solar system into the design adding 7.5kW of latest technology panels and a Fronius 5.0 AC coupled inverter.Even on a heavily overcast and rainy morning (today) the system supports modest household AC load and charges the batteries at a good rate. And power to spare in any sort of sun.The after sale service can't be beat either. Two courtesy calls after install just to check everything was working as 'advertised'. Last but not least the office staff were courteous and never failed to get back to me or pass on messages.I highly recommend Brenton and his team.Larry JamesWonga Beach FNQ

review_description: I requested six proposals for my solar upgrade and received six different solutions.  Several were clearly cookie cutter one size fits all proposals that got binned immediately, one didn't even listen to the brief,  then there are the installers who hear the basics then jump in before hearing the detail - Note to installers, if you can't be bothered even listening to what the customer is trying to achieve, what is the likelihood of them getting the solution they want?  This is where Greenline Solar stood out and secured my business.  During the development stage, Toby listened to what I wanted to achieve beyond basics of capacity, came up with a solution, put it to me to scrutinise, I got to ask questions that sometime required research on his part and eventually a shortlist of three proposals for me to choose from.  It was this level of collaboration, patience and commitment that got my signature.  Every part of the system could be qualified and justified.  Initially I thought I'd get a few quotes and boom job done, but the research phase took a lot longer than anticipated and I wouldn't change that because the result is fit for purpose.  After the groundwork  is done, the install is easy and the result is all but guaranteed.Jake and his install team turned up as planned, on time and worked like champs on what was in places a challenging install.  They asked questions rather than making assumptions, ran to schedule and cleaned up after themselves.  What more could you ask?If you take away one thing from this review it's this.  Any installer can install whatever panels, inverter, battery etc you spec based on your research or their opinion, then walk away - tick the boxes and away they go.  For some this is ok.  What you will get from Greenline Solar is that extra effort, time, commitment and integrity.  I'd use them again in a heartbeat and recommend them without reservation.

The Green Line Solar team was excellent throughout the whole process, from quoting on-site to delivery and providing me with a manual after commissioning. I have worked with many trades, and the Green Line team is very neat, clean, and clearly takes pride in the work they do. I felt confident during installation, as the communication was clear and concise. Any adjustments were advised and sought my permission before continuing.I was very happy with the backup and EV charging testing before handover. The filing of the necessary paperwork was quite seamless and well prepared, making admin a breeze. A big thank you to the Green Line Solar team!

I highly recommend Green Line Solar — a true 5-star experience from start to finish! Toby and Jake were an absolute pleasure to work with. Unlike some other companies, they never used high-pressure sales tactics. Toby took the time to patiently answer all of my questions, making sure I felt informed and confident every step of the way. On installation day, Jake and his team were efficient, professional, and made the whole process completely stress-free.If you’re considering going solar, Green Line Solar is the team to go with.

From the first phone call, Toby was very helpful, knowledgeable and responsive to our needs and queries. Explaining systems and requirements to us in a clear and patient manner that made our decision making process much easier. Also helped us organise a mains upgrade for optimal performance. On installation, Jake and the team were very professional and thorough, with great attention to detail and a quality result. From start to finish, the team were polite, punctual and available to answer questions. We are very happy with our system, and the process and journey from start to finish. We have seen a massive reduction in power bills and have already been consistently over 95% off grid due to the system’s efficiency. We highly recommend Green Line Solar for your solar and battery installation. Rob

After a lot of investigation online we chose Green Line Solar to install our rooftop PV and battery systems.  Throughout the process Toby and Jake from Green Line Solar provided clear advice and a very competitive quotation. Their subsequent attention to completing the installation in good time and of an excellent standard, was exemplary. We have no hesitation recommending Green Line Solar, and have done so to our family and friends.

I had Toby & Jake install my solar system almost 2 years ago. I was so impressed by the service (Toby took a lot of time to answer my many questions) that I went directly to Green Line Solar when the time came to add a battery. Toby again explained everything in plain language and got me a great deal on my new Sungrow battery.  Jake and his team just finished the install today (about 5 hours work). As always his team were polite, efficient and did a great job. I highly recommend Green Line Solar as they are easy to deal with, take the time to explain how solar works, and do a great job and are not pushy sales people. Thanks again guys

System: 39x Jinko 440w panels, 10kW Sungrow inverter, 12.8kWh Sungrow modular battery.When looking for quotes,  I spoke to several companies, and decided o go with Green Line Solar as they had really good pricing and speaking to Toby was straightforward and easy. He spoke in a way that was to my level of understanding and gave me a few different options, which was exactly what I was after. Green Line Solar handled most of the paperwork, with only Solar Victoria (for rebate, loans) needing to be done by myself online. The install was originally scheduled for early Feb the following year, but due to a supplier stock issue for a different brand, they were able to move up my install before Christmas, and I got some bonus STCs!On inspecting the house, Jake identified the best position for the inverter and battery, which happed to be where an old broken gas ducted heater was situated. He organized for a plumber to come out to disconnect the gas line and remove the heater. As part of the install, Jake provided concrete slabs and a cement sheet to cover the hole in the wall from the heater. The install happened over two wet days, and Jake and the guys on the roof took care to replace tiles each time it started raining. They kept me informed of when they needed to turn off the power, and kept that to a minimum. The install is very neat and tidy, the cable runs immaculate. Jake performed all the electrical checks, explained the changes to the switchboard, and introduced me to the Sungrow iSolarCloud app.I am very happy with the system, and all my dealings with Green Line Solar. Highly recommended!

We had an 11kw solar system installed with a 16kw battery which has been fantastic so far. The whole process from start to finish with Toby and Jake felt effortless, professional and simple. From Toby’s knowledge and advice to Jake’s attention to detail during the install. They both were always happy to answer any questions. Grid connection went ahead with very little input needed from me. If you want an honest team that deliver, Toby and Jake from GREENLINE Solar are your best pick.

Green Line Solar were the only Installers to visit the site - this was a major reason for finally choosing them. I was able to meet the staff & ask relevant questions. They were prompt, courteous & professional in all aspects of the job. They assisted with the rebate paperwork & helped with the grid connection after the install. I would recommend Green Line Solar.

The guys at Green Line Solar were fantastic to deal with.Regarding the sales and quoting process, Toby was realistic, polite, and non-pushy. Gave us plenty of time and space to review and think about the quotes we received. Quotes were also easy to read and more importantly, thorough.The installation by Jake and his apprentices was very smooth, pleasant, polite, and tidy as well. The finished product was very pleasing and symmetrical to look at as well. We were very pleased with the outcome of the install, despite having lots of warning labels and stickers all over the place due to regulations (which could not be avoided). We went with the battery and solar option, which had to be done over 2x days, but both days were very pleasant.In terms of customer service, Toby helped come back to tidy up a couple of things and added some additional labels which the inspector requested. So not the touch-and-go kind of company, which was good to know.

We have just had a 6.6KW Jinko solar system and Tesla Powerwall battery installed by the boys from Green Line Solar.The whole process was super easy and efficient from the initial quoting and installation advice provided by Toby right through to system installation and commissioning by Jake and his team.They did everything they promised to do, always turned up on time and completed our entire installation within two days.Jake took the time to explain the installation process and the final job looks terrific. The boys also left no mess for us to clean up.Their pricing was also very competitive compared to other solar quotes that we obtained.So if you are after a competitive deal backed up by great advice and service before, during and after the installation then give Green Line Solar an opportunity - you won't be disappointed!

After months of deliberating I am very happy I chose Green Line Solar for my PV and battery install. These guys take great pride in their work and understand that outstanding service is the key to happy customers.Toby is extremely knowledgeable with the different kinds of PV, inverter and battery hardware, and is very meticulous  in planning the location of the panels and inverter. Multiple options were offered, each carefully tailored to different scenarios of budget and PV use. There was never any pressure to buy, and all questions (of which I had many) were patiently answered. Prices were extremely competitive.Jake is an artist - his electrical work is immaculate. He took care to make sure that everything was lined up, square, and met his high standards. The rest of the install crew were diligent, careful and professional. Everything was cleaned up afterwards.The inspector was very happy with their work. All paperwork was submitted for grid connection soon after install was completed.

Toby and Jake and their team were fantastic with answering all the questions we had (there were many!), providing a quotation that was quick, informative, comprehensive, and competitive, and advising on the process of rebate-application. The installation went without a hitch (PV/battery/inverter) and Jake, Nusy and Teja worked like Trojans onsite to get the job completed despite rain and wind. They're very aware and respectful of customer's property and environment - no boombox! Post-install necessary software upgrades were organised, and we've had good advice on grid connection now the COES has been issued. We're rating Green Line Solar 'only' 5 stars because there's no option provided for 6!

Dave helped us choose the right system for our needs and our roof space.I would also like to pass on to you that we are very happy with the installers that came yesterday, they worked very hard all day.The weather wasn’t the best at times yesterday, but they continued the best they could until the weather cleared again.They were very professional and polite and they have a very good work ethic.

Very easy purchase and installation process with our new 10 kW Alpha ESS battery to the existing solar panel system we have at our home. Had several quotes for exactly same battery from other "big" solar companies but the quote from Samar Tech was easily the cheapest. Within 7 days my battery was competently installed by an independent contractor that Samar Tech always work with. The installation staff were very customer friendly and the overall installation was trouble free. I would highly recommend Samar Tech for battery and panel quotes and installations based solely on my experience of this occasion.
The team had done a wonderful job in our house and it’s working well and no issues at all...
Great service and installation, the team is professional and experienced

The quoting process was very helpful, the salesman knew his products and listened to what my wife and i were looking for and gave us a quote for the correct system, He was always ready to answer any Questions or ease any uncertainty we had.The Customer service and Administration team were up to date with everything in regards to organizing dates and times for the Installation of our system, they kept us in the loop in regards to what to expect  in regards to paperwork from our energy supplier to the final paperwork when the system went online.The installation crew that turned up were polite and quite knowledgeable about the product they were fitting, the workmanship is quite neat and tidy, they explained to us what the system was capable of and what to expect from it. There are still a few bugs to work out in regards to getting generator backup plug working correctly again but the technician is working hard to rectify the problem.
Have not yet installed the system, still organising finance etc..

We had Solbase quote and install 13kw of solar panels with a 16kw battery using Sigenergy components. The whole process went smoothly except for the issue of the NSW Gov removing the battery rebate due to the Federal Gov battery rebate but we came to an agreement on this. The system is working really well and I highly recommend Solbase to anyone looking for a solar system.

I received quotes from four companies, one of which was a company that friends had dealt with (I did not choose that company). I met with two suppliers, and went with Soltek as their representative was very knowledgeable and in particular, didn't try to 'upsell', even when I relayed suggestions from friends as to certain aspects of the system. He explained everything really well, with scenario examples. My knowledge in this field is minimal, to say the least, so I was grateful for his advice. The installation was done today and the installers were excellent. They arrived on time, were polite, friendly, and left absolutely no mess. They explained how the system works, showed me the app which monitors the system, and how that works, and answered all my questions. I highly recommend Soltek.However, I have raised with them the fact that their communication was a little lax between paying the deposit and the installation date. There was apparently a shortage of components which they were awaiting from China, which is reasonable, but I did raise my concerns with them that they should have kept me updated via email or a phone call, rather than me having to be the one to chase them. I think this is an administrative failing which should be addressed.Aside from this, I would still recommend Soltek.
Great customer service. Kept meep to speed with install progress. Helpful with supplier information.

It has been six months since the installation of the 13.2 KW SolarEdge and battery system. In short, everything has been running great. I work from home and have two Uni students here, “far too much”.  On one sunny day, I used the ducted air-con, oven, cook top, dishwasher, and washing machine and paid nothing.My feedback on the installers: I appreciated the pre-installation site visit. They were on time, professional, solutions-oriented and meticulous.  They left the place tidy and removed all materials.  Their communication was always clear, always taking the time to answer my questions, no matter how small. But most importantly, they were just great guys.As always, there were minor issues here and there. However, they took the initiative to engage with Head Office proactively and followed up so that all issues were promptly resolved.Communication and customer service pre and post installation with Head Office has been excellent.Regarding the sales process. The agent was always available for calls and questions throughout the quote process and determination of the correct system, coming in person to my house twice. Communication was clear, and he provided everything I needed to understand to make an informed decision. In short, it was straight talk, not "sales talk”So, touch wood, long may things continue.

Great company for the near-total amateur. They returned my calls promptly, answered my questions in language I could understand, then gave me time to research other outcomes and/or potential problems for myself. I appreciated them not doing the 'hard sell' and appreciated their no-fuss resolution to a problem that occurred in the initial installation of the solar panels. I followed up with battery installation and was just as impressed. The installers were very helpful- clear and patient in their explanations and made great suggestions how I could maximise the benefits of my new solar system. I have no doubt that if, in the future, I run into problems or forget some aspects managing the system, that they will provide  me with helpful advice and/or a speedy resolution. Thankyou Soltek

I had Damien attend to my house was very polite, he had walked me through all the options I could have of a solar and battery combination at my house with a hot water unit. I had settled on a red X system with a 20kw battery and a reclaim hot water tank.The install process was quick and the staff I had engaged with were friendly well informed and educated on the products.The office informed me very well of the Government rebates I was entitled too and always kept me posted on my install date.I had my install done by Blake he was a massive help very approachable throughout the day, keeping me posted on all activates that had to take place at my home, He alike the staff at Soltek and the technician walked me through the Red X system monitoring app as well.I have just received my bill with a family of 6 in winter and have been credited 20 bucks this a lot better compared to my average 600 dollar bill I was receiving preinstall.I Recommend the RED X system, Jinko panels and a hot water unit from Damien and his team.

Good luck with trying to get service from Soltek during warranty. Support and service during warranty is almost non existent.I have a problem since 07-Apr-2025, first reported to Soltek on 23-April, 2025. Have been following up almost on a weekly basis with Soltek Support person.No action yet, just excuses.May need to get Dept. of Fair Trading Involved

Panels were installed within a week of accepting their quote. Battery took 3 months before it was installed, though I was told it would be 6 weeks.An additional panel was installed afterwards, as they didn't maximise roof capacity initially (which was the brief), but his panel still isn't producing energy according to the app, despite weeks of trying to get it sorted.Emails are not replied to. When calling or messaging i typically get the response that their engineer is looking at it, but without anything actually being resolved.After installation our roof started leaking. We had a roofer come to inspect and he advised us a roof tile was broken due to the installation. Now we'll need them to take away one panel and fix this..It's great to have solar + battery, but it shouldn't be such a painful process.

Salesperson provided options for all the required panels, inverters and batteries.Left final decision up to me.Visited the site and ran through the options and provided detail quotes and fact sheets.Installation team were fantastic.App is easy to use.

Was provided was 3 separate options for systems including 3 types of panels and batteries. Was not told just to buy the most expensive one, and they listened to my requirements carefully.Installation was extremely efficient with panels and conduits installed by 11am, battery and wiring all completed by 1pm and full commissioning completed by 3pm.Power was being produced that day, battery fully topped up and I have barely used any power from the grid in the 21 days since installation.Electrician also gave advice on covering the inverter and battery to protect from the direct sunlight.

The job was a replacement of an old array of solar panels and inverter (17+ years old) with new panels and a battery.  Also included was the integration of an existing array of LG panels that are approximately six years old.The Soltek team did a fantastic job from start to finish. They arrived early and left late and most importantly left the site clean and spotless. The install for both the solar panels and battery went to plan with a minimum of fuss and bother and was a very professional neat and tidy job. Very happy with the outcome.

We had previously used this installer for our original solar system some 8 years ago. We thought we'd use them again to add on new solar panels, upgrade the inverter and install a battery. Unfortunately this time round, it was such a bad experience!Looking back on it all, the installation team didn't seem to be too experienced and the process all seemed a bit piece-meal. The electricians kept having to call back to the head office to get instructions on what to do and how to install things... this should have been a warning sign, but since our previous installation all went well, we didn't think too much of it at the time and trusted the company and their staff (mistake number 1). One of the installers even fell through an awning during the installation (which he shouldn't have been stepping on in the first place!) Thankfully he wasn't too injured!When the job wasn't completely done (as the installers needed to come back later in the week to complete some small tasks), Soltek was quite forceful in demanding the remainder of the payment be sent through despite not completing all the work. As they had provided good customer service previously and as the bulk of the installation was done, I trusted that they would follow up in a timely fashion and get all the work done, so I proceeded (foolishly) to pay the remainder of the balance. Boy was that a bad move! (mistake number 2)After having the battery installed, the house was consuming twice as much energy whenever the battery was being used. When we tried to contact Soltek about this, they completely disregarded our concerns, outright lied to us that the system was working correctly when it wasn't, and then went on to blame SolarEdge for the system malfunctioning... a brand new inverter and battery which was incorrectly installed by Soltek! They didn't have the manpower, technical knowledge or decency to properly troubleshoot the issue with us or SolarEdge. We had to contact SolarEdge ourselves to escalate the issue further. Eventually (1-2 months later) SolarEdge thankfully sent out their own technician to review the installation as the Soltek worker that was sent out "couldn't find any problems with the installation". Indeed the system was incorrectly installed (incorrectly wired) and it wasn't even initialised properly! The SolarEdge technician was able to promptly diagnose and fix the wiring and now, finally, the system is working as it was designed to.3-4 months on, we still have cracked roof tiles that have not been replaced (we have spare tiles ready), the system layout still has not been updated with SolarEdge, and radio silence from them about when they would complete the remaining work.We wished that we could give glowing reviews to Soltek, as our original experience with this company was very positive, however 8 years on, it seems that they no longer value their customers - poor customer service, poor after sales support, poor communication, outright lies after receiving payment for a botched install.
Quoting was smooth and the ensuing negotiations pleasing. Commitments were kept and timelines adhered to. Both the salesperson and the installer did an excellent job and we are now up and running.

Sales rep Damien was an engineer who had detailed knowledge of all panel, inverter and battery options.  Quote included three panel / inverter options and three battery options.  Discussed pros / cons of each option.  Installation in one day was seamless with strong lead-hand Patrick who took care of the details.  Very good after sales service including set-up of SolarEdge monitoring system on computer and phone.  All paperwork with retailer was handled by Soltek including installation of smart meter.

Mike at Soltek was great to deal with. Competitive pricing and solid information provided in relation to any queries. Very timely and extremely professional installation - they did a great job in a "busy" area. A real pleasure to work with on this project. Would strongly recommend -  thanks Finn and team for the steer!

The sales quoting process was quick and succinct.All details of the various solar panels and inverters and batteries were clearly written and tabulated.It made choosing the right solar panels for my home easier.The technicians were punctual. They were polite and friendly. Did a good job. They were careful not to break any tiles and they cleaned up after their work.The technician showed me how to turn off the inverter and how to check the inverter status. He answered my various questions.They helped organize the grid connection after the installation.There was a small problem with the battery not talking to the inverter but Soltekenergy helped rectify it.

Every aspect from the initial quote through to the actual panel installation with Soltek has been efficient, professionally conducted and well communicated. The quoting process was clear, thoroughly informative, not just "sales talk". Only waited about a week before a very knowledgeable team arrived to do the installation. They were well organised, polite, kept us informed of each step they were doing and finished the job to a very high standard.Customer service and followup in arranging grid connection etc with our provider has been excellent.Overall, we could not fault the quality of the product we purchased nor the service we received from Soltek.

The sales consultant was punctual, polite and patient. He answered  my questions and informed me of all the options available to me, in terms of cost and quality, for both panels and inverters. And then followed up with a detailed written quotation.The installers were polite, hardworking, tidy and professional, staying til early evening to finish the install on the same day.With regard to the grid connection, I did need to chase that up, but once i called them, they were very prompt in putting in the request to my provider.Overall, I am very satisfied with my experience with Soltek

All three companies that I obtained quotes from had excellent and very responsive salespeople.  Soltek's salesman was marginally better with his answers to technical questions and persuaded us to buy a Solar Edge string system with optimisers instead of an Enphase micro-inverter system.  (Another company had also recommended a string system with optimisers over a micro-inverter system.)  The presentation of Soltek's quote for several alternative systems, with equipment from various manufacturers, showed their technical features and prices in the way that made it easiest to compare them.  Finally, Soltek agreed to a discount to match another company's quote.Just before accepting the quote, I realised that a small group of PV panels on the western roof might be vulnerable to shadow from a chimney and a basketball backboard.  Soltek's salesman proposed a modified positioning of those panels, but no decision was made.Our installation was booked to start at 9 am on a Thursday, as I had told Soltek that that was the only day that I could be on site.  At 10 am I called Soltek to find out why nobody had turned up.  It emerged that, because on the Tuesday rain had been predicted for the Thursday, Soltek had decided to postpone installation to the Friday.  However, the installation supervisor had forgotten to message me to tell me that.Because I could not be present on the Friday and I needed to know where Soltek planned to place the panels on the western roof and the battery, the installation supervisor reluctantly agreed to visit the site on the Thursday afternoon.  The supervisor wanted me, instead of him, to make the final decision on where to place the panels on the western roof.  I said that I would leave it to him to work it out with the salesman, as I would rely on Soltek's technical expertise.  The positioning of the battery was decided largely because the only alternative position would have incurred additional cost, which I had not been told to expect.The installation appeared to have been carried out well.  Everything was very neat.Once the installation was complete, I received an email inviting me to register for Solar Edge's online monitoring app.  To my surprise, it referred to a 10.14kW system, not a 13.33kW system.  (The generation system is 13.33kW and the battery is 10.14kW.)  I registered and could immediately see how the system was performing.The next day I received another email inviting me to register for Solar Edge's online monitoring app, this time referring to a 13.33kW system. I emailed Soltek about this and was told that the person who sent the second invitation wasn't aware that someone else at Soltek had already sent me an invitation.  Subsequently, I asked both Soltek and Solar Edge which invitation I should accept, but so far neither of them have responded.A week after the system was installed, when I was away for a few days, the monitoring app showed that the system had stopped generating.  When I got back home I took photographs of the inverter (which has 3 indicator lights, but nothing to say what they mean) and my electrical switch box and emailed them to Soltek, asking for advice on whether the system was working and, if not, how to make it work.  Soltek directed me to the part of the monitoring app that re-establishes the connection between the system and the internet.  When I couldn't reconnect the system, Soltek referred me to Solar Edge's support.My conversations with Solar Edge's support ended with it saying that I needed to get my internet service provider to reconfigure my modem (router).  I spent a lot of time communicating with my ISP, but couldn't achieve what Solar Edge said that it needed.Several more communications with Solar Edge and Soltek ended with each of them referring me back to the other to solve the problem.Eventually I carried out an online search and found another installer's advice on how to restart a Solar Edge system.  Following those instructions, I opened my electrical switch box and - with a bit more research - worked out that the generation system had tripped the main switch, so the Solar Edge system was not working at all.  Once I switched it back on, I was able to reconnect the monitoring system and see (a) that the generating system had not worked for about a week and (b) it was now working.The net result of all of this was that I was left with the impression that, once the system had been installed and I had paid for it, Soltek didn't want to be involved any more.  Apart from directing me to Solar Edge support, it simply didn't answer my questions.  Worst of all, it was obvious that Soltek's engineer had not bothered to look at the photos I emailed to Soltek when I got back home, from which she could have seen immediately that the system was switched off.  (It's extraordinary that Soltek didn't raise that as a thing to check as soon as I contacted it.)Solar Edge's support also missed the obvious check to find out whether the system was on or off.  Its advice to have my ISP reconfigure my modem (router) was obviously wrong.The bottom line: I am happy with the Solar Edge system, which is working well.  However, I've learned that it's largely up to me to understand how to manage the system and solve problems, with unreliable support from Solar Ege and no support from Soltek.

Daniel the energy consultant actually came to premises before quoting. Was knowledgeable about the options and provided quotes for different panels etc.Installation flawless. Went to schedule.Only one issue to do with mis communication about existence of battery and requiring a special part for 3 phase they didn't have on the day. Was installed the next day..This installation was an expansion of existing system installed in 2018.

Sales/quote process was clear and effectiveInstallation struck an initial snag because installer did not want to install the inverter in the location I had agreed to with the sales person, but it was sorted out satisfactorily.Customer service was extremely supportive and ran smoothly

The process was very easy, the team was always contactable and the experts were professional and very helpful. The sales person talked through all the options and provided different quotes as needed. The installation was easy and they walked me through it and kept me updated. High standard of work and a professional job, even handling the complexities of the site with a small working area.

I can’t rave enough about Soltek Energy. They have gone above and beyond at every step to give us a great deal, brilliant product and excellent service. Damien and his team are awesome and are utmost professionals. Super happy with our solar system, heat pump for our pool and battery. I highly recommend these guys for your solar solution. 10/10

I chose Soltek Energy for my install.  They told me that I had to install a 4 core and earth 16 mm cable from the garage, where the panels are installed, to the main switchboard 56 meters in total.  That is a heavy-duty cable in a domestic situation for sure.The reason to install this cable was, when you install 22 solar panels, as he insisted could be installed, you need two cable strings running to the main switchboard.  Only 21 panels were installed as the installers said the 22nd wasn’t allowed by the installation rules.  They didn’t mention that if the Enphase board were installed in the garage, close to the panels, only one string would be needed back to the main switchboard. That was exactly where the Soltek electrician installed it, in the garage.  If one does a calculation - 21 panels at 410-watt equals 8.61kW at 240V/36amp.  These panels facing north at 2 degrees angle will never produce 8.61kW, maybe 6.61kW on a good day with Enphase micro inverters, so more likely 29amp.  One string over 56 meters would be more than enough, even with the de rating over this distance.Therefore, I could have installed a 2 core and earth 16 square cable and saved $350.00.  By installing the Enphase board in the garage the electrician now had two spare 16 square ml cords to deal with (White and Blue), he installed these on the main earth bar.  Since when is it permissible to install any other colour of cable to the Earth bar other than Yellow/Green?One ADC310T circuit breaker, was removed and not returned to owner.The switchboard was left unlocked at the top, as the left locking point has been damaged.  The switchboard needs replacing, as it no longer can be secured and locked.I had three panels installed on the back roof of the garage facing south. The back bracket is installed at such an angle as it’s pulling the right hand corner down and is putting a lot of strain on the panel.How difficult is it to locate and drill into the middle of a wood support beam when clearly visible from underneath. My Enphase PV system and Tesla Powerwall 2 battery was sold to me by Solarworx and installed by Thoroughtec around 2020. An initial 9.6kW PV system was installed followed shortly after that by a Tesla Powerwall 2 battery. Additional panels were installed in 2022 to bring PV system up to 14.4kW- Installation by Adrian at Thoroughtec was professional and I can't fault the installation.- before the system was installed Solarworx requested that I put up a review of the installation before it had actually been done. It seemed like a strange request at the time but in good faith I did so. That review has since been taken down at my request.- During a prolonged outage my system went fully offline. I had been led to believe that the system was configured to charge the battery from one third of the PV panels during a grid outage. Upon inquiry to Solarworx they told me that Tesla systems had been shut down by Tesla on orders from SAPN. While servicing the system at a later date the technician informed me that the battery didn't charge during the blackout because the system hadn't been configured to do so.- During installation of the Tesla battery two CT sensors were removed from the Enphase system and went missing. Inquiries to SolaWorx as to the whereabouts of the missing CTs (I paid for them) were met with evasive answers. During one phone call with the director they assured me that they had the CTs sitting on the car seat next to them as we spoke and they'd be delivered that day. They never turned up.  I eventually received 2 CTs in the mail after several emails and texts.- During the adding of the additional panels mapping of the extra panels on to the Enphase system was not done. I never got a straight answer from either Solaworx or installer as to why this hadn't been done. After several requests to Solaworx to get the mapping done I approached the installer directly and they eventually mapped the panels.- In late 2023 a repeatedly tripping battery isolation circuit breaker was traced to a melted battery AC harness connector. I paid a service person to trouble shoot the problem after being told there'd be a 15 day wait by Tesla before the problem could be looked at. I made Solaworx and Thoroughtec aware of the issue via email. Heard nothing back from Solaworx but got a response from Thoroughtec.- In early 2024 an intermittent issue with the neurio meter started occurring. I didn't bother attempting to get the issue resolved by Solarworx based on my experiences with them up to that point. Since then I have been trying to get the issue resolved via direct contact with Tesla, and via Thoroughtec....so far with no resolution.- to his credit Adrian at Thoroughtec has tried his best to help me out even though the onus should be on Solarworx to resolve my issues. I can't fault the installer.- My advice to anyone considering PV or a battery...only deal with a company that does the actual installation. Avoid doing business with salesmen who then subcontract out the installation to other parties. Overall my experiences with Solarworx were very disappointing and I wouldn't recommend the company to anyone.- I see a number of glowing recent reviews from people who have had Sigenergy systems installed by Solarworx. Good luck and hope you don't have any issues with those systems. If you have any issues theres a high chance you will like me end up having to deal with the equipment manufacturer and/or the installers.

I plugged in my laptop and tested both the ports, both were fine.  As I plugged the inverters back in, I noticed that the hybrid connected intermittently as I moved the cable.  I reterminated the Ethernet cable (I have worked in the comms industry for some time) and the system has been up and running since!For anyone with no knowledge of comms, they would still be running around in circles with this level of supportStandard of installation very poorStandard of Service very weak knowledge of the product when there are issuesBeware the claims made by RACV Solar - I wouldn't wish what happened to me on anyone else
